It explores the likelihood of human behaviour when such crime is happening to us, blurring the lines between good and bad **** a 153 minute movie, the story does unfolds at a slow and solemn pace (which hurts the film and might bore some audiences) but the dramatic scenes performed by the main cast members in the film will keep you engaged. Hugh Jackman and Jack Gyllenhaal both giving intense, Oscar-worthy performances here, defining and developing their characters with various layers of emotions: affection, anger, grief, empathy, guilt...throughout the **** film's atmosphere, heavy rains, stormy days and icy cold winter managed to create a dark, dreadful environment to make up the dreary and haunting mood in the film. Every violent action taken by the characters are acts of desperation given that they are running out of time. If, after the Dune duology and Blade Runner 2049, you're craving something intense and want to see another Villeneuve film, a movie from a different decade about abduction in the American deep is exactly what you need. Memento Memento Some memories are best forgotten. Mystery Thriller Christopher Nolan Guy Pearce Carrie-Anne Moss Joe Pantoliano Mark Boone Junior Russ Fega Jorja Fox Stephen Tobolowsky Harriet Sansom Harris Thomas Lennon Callum Keith Rennie Leonard Shelby is tracking down the man who raped and murdered his wife. The difficulty of locating his wife's killer, however, is compounded by the fact that he suffers from a rare, untreatable form of short-term memory loss. Although he can recall details of life before his accident, Leonard cannot remember what happened fifteen minutes ago, where he's going, or why. This film reminds me somewhat of the themes so dear to Sacks, foremost among them memory and its dysfunctions, in this case, the protagonist's anterograde amnesia. It's genuinely fascinating to observe the practical implications and complications for someone who can retain memories only up to a certain point in their life, a point now firmly in the past. I also appreciated how the film serves as a celebratory monument to karma, which spares no one. I found the way the film is constructed admirable, it's a return to the past, defluidified and fragmentary. The set design, screenplay, and staging are all carefully crafted. This is a film worth watching at least once in a lifetime. Very particular film for the type of development. The plot is based entirely on the memory problems of the protagonist which are reproduced in a very effective way contributing to making the story mysterious and incomprehensible to the viewer as it happens to the protagonist. Perhaps it could have been slightly clearer in the ending where the truth is revealed to the viewer, but overall it remains a very particular and truly well done film Memento is just a fantastic film as Christopher Nolan has produced a syringe that injects doses that you wouldn’t mainly think what is going to happen. After stretching his legs in the arthouse scene with 1998's Following, Christopher Nolan gets a little more mainstream in this swervy, concept-rich tale of amnesiac vengeance. Guy Pearce plays a man with short-term memory loss, constantly overwriting the VHS tape of his near-past as he tracks a nameless, faceless killer. He employs some blunt methods for retaining important information - hand-written notes and Polaroids for loose facts, tattoos for solid truths - but when you're operating on such a short timer (the dreaded memory wipe seems to occur every ten minutes), I suppose you've got to take what you can get, even if it makes you a target for manipulation.

The whole fable unfolds in a sort of stuttered reverse, immediately revealing the plot's ending before slowly walking back to its beginning, which leaves the viewer feeling almost as handicapped as Pearce. It's an early example of Nolan's experimental nature, his interest in tinkering with traditional storytelling formats to bend viewers' perceptions, and it works just as well here as we might expect from his later works. At each intersection, we're forced to second-guess everything we thought we knew, which continually changes the context of that first ten minute chunk. Our trust is earned, betrayed, diverted and rehabilitated.

Sure, sometimes it feels like this is more about the experiment than the plot (for all its ambition, the actual story is very small-scale), but measured conceptual risk carries a lot of weight with me and Memento is a verifiable playground for such things. It's as effective a "walk a mile in my shoes" experience as any I've seen on the big screen, and a large part of that can be credited to the Nolan brothers' peculiar knack for outside-the-box cinematic creativity. this is my seventh favorite film due to it solidifying nolan as one of the greatest directers in the world with its great storytelling design J’écris vite cette critique avant de l’avoir oubliée : j’ai la cervelle en vrac à force de remettre à l’endroit ce film à l’envers, car le pire c’est que des morceaux de Memento tiennent la route avec d’autres morceaux et lorsqu’on croit avoir recollé l’ensemble, d’autres morceaux nous échappent…

Cars 3 maintains Pixar's high animation standards, with polished visuals that gleam like a freshly waxed paint job. The racing sequences are particularly well-executed, capturing the speed and intensity of the track. However, it's not a groundbreaking leap forward from the first film, feeling more like a pit stop for the animation studio rather than a triumphant return to form.

Soundtrack:

Story and Characters
Let's talk about the narrative. "Cars 3" brings Lightning McQueen back into the driver's seat, but this time he's facing the inevitable: aging and newer, sleeker models. The film attempts to explore themes of mentorship, legacy, and the passage of time, injecting some much-needed depth into the series. However, the narrative feels somewhat formulaic, hitting familiar beats that we've seen in countless sports movies. It's like they took a page from the underdog playbook and followed it to the letter.

Themes
Now, the themes. Cars 3 tries to deliver a message about the importance of passing the torch, but it occasionally veers into overly sentimental territory. 

The film's attempt to balance nostalgia with a fresh perspective is commendable, but it doesn't quite achieve the emotional resonance of Pixar's more impactful **** the grand Pixar spectrum, "Cars 3" is a respectable comeback after the wrong turn of "Cars 2." It steers the franchise back towards the emotional resonance that Pixar is known for, even if it doesn't break any new ground. 

It's a solid conclusion to the trilogy, giving Lightning McQueen a fitting farewell lap. It's a competent sequel that puts the series back on track, but it lacks the innovative spark of Pixar's best work.

Zack Snyder’s Justice League isn’t just a director’s cut—it’s a resurrection, a reclamation, and a full-blown mythological epic that puts heart, grandeur, and vision back at the center of the DCEU.

Clocking in at a bold 4 hours, this is no mindless popcorn flick. It’s an operatic saga worthy of the gods it portrays. Snyder unleashes his full creative arsenal—dreamlike visuals, raw emotion, and thunderous scale—to craft a superhero film that dares to be art. It's Tolkien by way of Kirby; Wagner conducted by Junkie XL.

Every hero is given the arc they deserve. Ben Affleck’s Batman trades brooding nihilism for hope. Henry Cavill’s Superman, reborn in black, embodies mythic gravitas. Gal Gadot’s Wonder Woman slashes through terrorists and parademons with equal conviction, while Ezra Miller’s Flash gets the single most beautiful time-travel sequence ever seen in a comic book film. Ray Fisher’s Cyborg transforms from narrative footnote to the soul of the League.



The story breathes. It mourns. It builds. Scenes that were once butchered are now fully realized—Steppenwolf has motivation, Darkseid looms like a cosmic shadow, and every frame oozes purpose. Even the much-debated 4:3 aspect ratio turns out to be a stroke of genius, giving the film the feel of a living graphic novel.

Yes, it’s indulgent. Yes, it’s dark. And yes, it’s unapologetically Snyder—but that’s exactly what elevates it above the generic crowd of formulaic blockbusters. This is a vision uncompromised.

Rewatching Now You See Me after all these years, still captivated by its tight and sharp narrative pacing, visually dazzling scenes, and the cleverly crafted magic sequences. The mystery unfolds in a way that keeps you guessing, with some moments that feel genuinely clever and others that rely on misdirection. While the twist works, it feels like it was designed more for shock value than something deeply layered, but it still delivers on the fun factor.

The directing does a solid job of balancing action with the illusion-based storytelling, making each trick feel larger than life. The cinematography leans into the sleek and stylish, using dynamic camera movements that enhance the sense of spectacle. There’s a good rhythm to the editing, making sure the pacing never drags, though some moments feel a little too quick, as if rushing to the next big trick. The sound design and score add to the energy, keeping the excitement high throughout.

Acting-wise, the cast is strong, with Jesse Eisenberg, Woody Harrelson, Isla Fisher, and Dave Franco each bringing distinct personalities to the group. Mark Ruffalo plays his role well, though his character sometimes feels overshadowed by the magicians. Morgan Freeman and Michael Caine add weight to the film, though Freeman, as always, feels like he’s playing a version of himself. Mélanie Laurent is a welcome addition, though her role is somewhat underdeveloped. The script is sharp, filled with witty dialogue and a sense of mystery that works well for this type of film. While it may not be a deeply thought-provoking movie, it’s a stylish and enjoyable ride that keeps you entertained throughout.

This time he's squared up against a reimagined Blofeld, played by a characteristically snooty, Machiavellian Christoph Waltz. That seems like good casting on the surface, but in practice it's something of an awkward fit.

Perhaps the villain's uninspired master plan has something to do with his struggles. I know the threats of leaked personal data and unwarranted surveillance are hot topics in today's political spectrum, but this hardly seems like a grand scheme worthy of a vast, international criminal enterprise and the dogged attention of MI-6. Still, Bond and Blofeld find a way to spin that into a deranged torture scene, giant fireballs in the desert and a helicopter chase through the heart of London, so props for navigating such a bizarre progression.

In fact, each of Spectre's action scenes are spectacular when removed from the larger narrative. We're rarely more than ten or fifteen minutes from the next chase via land, sea or air, and though we revisit several vehicles and locations, each pursuit feels fresh and original. We skim from one location to the next like a sightseeing tour, but that often seems like it's more for show than to further the story.

When Cletus bites Eddie and ingests Venom’s blood, he transforms into Carnage—a red, more powerful symbiote fueled by Cletus’s murderous rage. Their escape and subsequent reunion with Shriek at Ravencroft lead to a visually stunning climax, where the "Black Bride" and "Red Groom" dynamic is brought to life with impressive art **** film also doubles down on the quirky, domestic comedy between Eddie and Venom. From Venom acting like a pining ex-lover and cooking breakfast to his hilarious "coming out" speech at an LGBTQ party where he declares his freedom from "Eddie’s closet," the duo’s chemistry remains the franchise's greatest strength. While the plot has its share of conveniences—like Venom being able to draw detailed crime scenes from memory or Cletus having elite hacking skills—the character interactions keep it engaging. Supporting players like Anne and her fiancé Dan are utilized well, with Dan finally earning Venom’s respect through his bravery. Despite a somewhat rushed finale where Carnage is outmatched by the sonic counter of his own partner, the movie delivers a fun, chaotic ride that culminates in a major multiverse tease, hinting at a vast "hive mind" of knowledge spanning billions of light-years. A symbiotic sequel that lacks bite

Venom: Let There Be Carnage tries to build on what worked in its predecessor, but collapses under its own chaotic execution. The film’s strongest element remains the dynamic between Eddie Brock and Venom. Their constant bickering and snappy inner dialogue provide most of the humor and energy, and Tom Hardy once again fully commits to the absurdity of the role, which makes these moments genuinely entertaining.

Outside of that central relationship, the film struggles badly. The pacing is so rushed that there is barely any room for characters or ideas to breathe, making the entire experience feel undercooked. The romance subplot once again feels forced and unnecessary, existing more out of obligation than narrative logic. Carnage, despite being one of Venom’s most iconic adversaries, is a major disappointment. His design leans toward a strange fungal aesthetic rather than a menacing alien presence, and his combat style quickly becomes excessive in a way that feels more silly than threatening. None of the antagonists are given enough depth to feel compelling, leaving their motivations shallow and forgettable.

While the film carries over some of the humor and visual energy of the first Venom, it lacks any sense of balance or purpose. What remains is a loud, frantic sequel that mistakes speed and spectacle for substance, resulting in an experience that feels more exhausting than fun and leaves little reason to revisit it once the credits roll. Tom Hardy really plays a great Venom, and if Venom himself wasn't such a loser, or this film was actually folded into the MCU this could be a great series. Woody Harrelson makes for a fun and fantastic Carnage. This movie is arguably better than the first, and the fight scenes are a lot easier to watch and understand than the fight scenes between Venom and Riot in the first film. If you'd have told me a super hero film directed by Andy Serkis featuring Tom Hardy and Woody H would be mediocre, I would have laughed in your face. However, some how it happened. The early 2000s superhero quirk of the original Venom is lost here as it tries to build and expand it's Sony Universe. This is the issue Sony seems to always fall short on (Exampe: Amazing Spiderman 2 being more about setting up a universe than actually focussing on Spiderman). 

It was all down hill from here. Very classic film for its genre. Compared to the previous chapter, the plot is more refined but less effective, making the film less fun than the previous one and therefore less successful. A beautiful and wonderful movie and the ending is very happy And a great representation from Tom Hardy "Venom: Let There Be Carnage," was...  A lot like the first movie......  Which means it was just O.K.:  They definitely delivered on the Venom vs Carnage fight, but that was about it.  Shriek felt nonexistent throughout most of the film, and Woody Harrelson playing the role of Carnage felt like a waste of his talents.

Tom Hardy breathed tons of life into this film and it would have **** without him (much like the first one).  This is another “meh” Marvel movie that exists almost exclusively for the mid-credits reveal (Which was pretty cool) The interplay between Eddy and Venom is what gives the movie life. It provides humor in an anantagonistic odd couple relationship on steroids. Once we get to the Carnage portion and showdown, it becomes more of a cgi mess. Venom: Let There Be Carnage" is a fun and fast superhero movie. It's short, only 90 minutes, but still full of exciting action and silly moments. The movie is about Venom and his wild adventures, but it also has a sweet story about friendship and love. It’s not perfect, but if you like action, laughs, and a little bit of craziness, this movie is a great choice!

395.title: Luca

metadata.tagline: Prepare for an unforgettable trip.

395.rich_text:
Luca Luca Prepare for an unforgettable trip. Animation Comedy Fantasy Family Drama Enrico Casarosa Jacob Tremblay Jack Dylan Grazer Emma Berman Saverio Raimondo Maya Rudolph Marco Barricelli Jim Gaffigan Peter Sohn Lorenzo Crisci Marina Massironi Luca and his best friend Alberto experience an unforgettable summer on the Italian Riviera. But all the fun is threatened by a deeply-held secret: they are sea monsters from another world just below the water’s surface. "실렌시오 브루노!"내가 나라면, 이 곳이 이 곳이라면, 지금 바로 최선을 다해 헤엄쳐!한 명은, 한 마을은, 어쩌면 나를 품어줄지도 모르니까240611 (3.5)-1. 서로를 괴물이라고 생각하는 육지생물과 해양생물. 다르다는 건 무서운 거고 그래서 필요없는 싸움이 생긴다2. 이탈리아를 상징하는 것이 많이 나와서 재미있었다 .파스타, 젤라또, 에스프레소, 피노키오, 오토바이, 자전거3. 부모를 잃은 알베르토를 어떻게 알아보고 자식을 잃은 줄리에타 아버지가 정을 줬는지 뭉클 Um filme que eu recomendo muito,ainda mais para quem ama filmes de deixar o coraçãomais confortável,e sinceramente,se tornou um dos meus filmes favoritos de animação. Luca é uma daquelas animações que conquistam pelo coração. Ele não tenta ser grandioso ou épico—sua força está na simplicidade e na autenticidade das relações entre os personagens. Com um visual deslumbrante, uma trilha sonora envolvente e uma história sincera sobre amizade e crescimento, o filme prova que nem toda obra-prima precisa ser complexa.100/100. Porque algumas histórias são perfeitas exatamente como são. I absolutely loved Luca! This movie has such a sweet, genuine vibe that makes it feel both nostalgic and refreshing. It’s set on the Italian Riviera, which looks incredible in Pixar’s animation. You can almost feel the warmth of the sun and the coolness of the water. But what really makes Luca stand out is the story. It’s not just about sea monsters and human worlds; it’s about friendship, embracing who you are, and facing fears with the help of people who care about you. It’s such a meaningful, feel-good movie without ever trying too hard. There’s a real charm to it that reminds me of childhood summers and simple joys. Honestly, I think it’s super underrated in Pixar’s lineup—maybe it didn’t get the attention of some other Pixar films, but it deserves every bit of praise. Luca is the kind of movie that quietly warms your heart, and I’d recommend it to anyone who wants something cute, thoughtful, and uplifting. A great movie especially for family’s and children, it has occasional emotional scenes and a good story. Recommend 8/10 A secret race of mer-people live their quiet lives off the Italian coast and raise their quiet children to fear the surface-dwelling monsters that sometimes pass overhead in wooden rowing machines. Luca is one such good boy, obediently spooked by what lies above, but also a little intrigued by the promise of a bigger, broader, brighter world. When he befriends another, more daring child, the two begin testing limits. Limits imposed by their parents and society, but also those within themselves. They push each other like any good, close, young friends, bolder together than they'd ever be alone, and share the pleasures of discovery that result.

What follows is a beautiful coming of age story, set in the lush summer of a sleepy seaside Mediterranean village during the mid-twentieth century. It embodies the awestruck sense of limitless possibility that typifies the nearing of adolescence, as well as the golden warmth and sure, steady pacing of Italian cinema. Luca isn't afraid to linger in a moment, to better appreciate its beauty, and the masters at Pixar have once again outdone themselves in this respect. It feels redundant to mention at this point, but these guys know what it takes to make the screen come alive, while also showing enough restraint to avoid overloading the senses. Just another entry in a long line of stunners. The arching storyline is similarly rich, simple and effective. There's a cocky bully-type in town, a resilient young girl tired of taking his crap and a triathlon proving ground (of sorts), plus the natural tension surrounding the transformed sea-kids' fear of discovery. Nothing groundbreaking, really, but it's all efficiently managed with a good sense of timing, a playful spirit and a whole sackful of delicious regional flavor.

I wouldn't put this one on a pedestal beside Toy Story 3 or Wall-E, but it's comfortably around the top of the next tier. Light, beautiful, warm-hearted and hopeful... just like a well-spent summer vacation. Gorgeous, moody, immaculate vibes.  I just want to dive into this movie and eat fish pasta with the crusty sailor dad forever.  The cast is incredible.  Leads are fantastic, but the supporting cast also rules.  Jim Gaffigan and Maya Rudolph make for one of the quietest but best parent duos in cinema.  Emma Berman, Saverio Raimondo, and Marco Barricelli should be stars.  My kids watched this movie on end for months.  I consider myself (and my sanity) fortunate that they have such fine taste.  A bildungsroman to stand with the best of them. This movie has excellent animation and good voice acting, however, this kind of plot has been done so many times before, and better I might add. Still, the movie itself does provide enough entertainment to keep the interest of the audience for the 98 minute runtime. Definición de buena película, entretenida y básica en algunos aspectos. Pero aun con todo eso logra mantenerse interesante. Hoy en día es muy complicado hacer adaptaciones que logren entretener al público por completo, ya que en muchas películas hay demasiada propaganda de por medio. Este no es el caso.
Tiene muchas similitudes con otras películas de Disney, como es el caso de La sirenita y Valiente. La búsqueda del conocimiento y el saber, la libertad, el temor a lo desconocido y todo lo que conlleva conocer una nueva parte del mundo, es lo que conforma a esta nueva obra de Pixar.
En muchas críticas leí que decían que es una película que carecía de alma. Pero yo creo que alma tienen todas las películas, cada una a su propia manera.
Considero que hoy en día en esta sociedad tan cambiante, a muchos de nosotros nos falta ese poquito de Luca. The Italian summer vibed atmosphere with accordian music and Top tier animation and sound with visually pleasing scenaries it was calming. The story was decent the pacing is good, the characters were sweet, the aspect of above sea life for sea monsters there back and forth water spillings and the twist of them to others was quite intriguing, The last half was sweet, surprising and entertaining, Overall the mixture of rowdy kid as villian and underdog team of friends with sweet family angle and the racing it was usual recipie but executed amazingly, Its was an Amazing Movie.

396.title: mother!

metadata.tagline: Seeing is believing.

396.rich_text:
mother! mother! Seeing is believing. Horror Drama Darren Aronofsky Jennifer Lawrence Javier Bardem Ed Harris Michelle Pfeiffer Brian Gleeson Domhnall Gleeson Jovan Adepo Amanda Chiu Patricia Summersett Eric Davis A couple's relationship is tested when uninvited guests arrive at their home, disrupting their tranquil existence. Mother poses an enigma, both for the narrative and for the viewer, and the enigma isn't that complicated; A young man with an intellectual disability is charged with murder.
The clues point to him, and there are reasons to believe it, but there are also reasons not to do it, and these fall on the mother, totally willing to try and show it.
So the deal is to find out if he did it or if he didn't Fortunately the film doesn't provide easy answers, and this is appreciated because it doesn't try to complicate the plot more than it should.
It's evident that there is a good argumentative construction, and Bong Joon-ho knows how to sustain the tension without overstretching the viewer's patience.

Mother is not what it appears to be, and it's deceptive enough without trying to anticipate your own guesswork, and that's an incredibly difficult thing to do. Especially when it comes to thrillers.
But this isn't your conventional affair, and for that I thank the director. C'est une mère-poule névropathe aux 400 coups pour son rejeton carrément débile sur les bords (et au milieu) qui se retrouve au très grand insu de son plein gré mêlé à une histoire de meurtre... Complètement à côté de ses pompes, ce jeune rain man dort avec sa maman (sic !) et son "meilleur" pote est un petit loubard à la petite semaine.

Partant de là, ce merdier dramatico-psycho-social est délayé sur deux plombes qui semblent en durer six... je ne sais pas sur quoi ça débouche parce que je me suis endormi et que j'ai tiré la chasse. A noter que c'est fréquemment filmé caméra à l'épaule, ce qui file la nausée et le mal de mer(de). De ce que j'ai vu, la maman paniquée plutôt toquée et frappadingue met tout en oeuvre pour aider son fils mongolo... mais de toute façon, on a déjà zappé cette daube coréenne, cela va sans dire ! With Mother, Bong Joon Ho delivers another strange genre blend. Mother is a crime movie, but it is also a character study and in parts a psychological thriller. The movie first follows Do-Joon (Won Bin), the mentally challenged young adult son of a single mom (Kim Hye-ja). Do-Joon is easily duped and has the mental capacities of middle to an early high schooler, despite being in his twenties. The narrative shift focus to the mother after Do-Joon is convicted of the murder of a young girl. Shortly before her murder, Do-Joon was drunkenly returning home, vaguely following her, because he liked her. What follows is the epic journey of a single mom, downtrodden by media, society, and the economy, trying to prove her son’s innocence and catch the real culprit. The movie takes this somewhat simple narrative and uses it to explore the faults with the criminal justice system, class warfare, and ableism. Just when the viewer thinks they have caught onto where the movie is going, the movie reveals new details subverting the narrative and tropes. Mother has many things to say, but the most potent of which is a meta-critique given at the last moment. Mother shows the power that enough dedication to a task can have, but it also shows the futility and consequences of the dedication. Bong Joon Ho has arguably the best film of 2019-Parasite.  I like Okja the best so far.  This is nicely photographed and acted.  There are a lot of movies and shows lately, if it is not engaging halfway through i quit.  made it halfway. Supported by amazing acting performances, a good soundtrack, beautiful cinematography and an interesting story that keeps you guessing until the gut wrenching finale, Mother deserves to be seen. "Mother" is an alluring piece of work, an artful mystery that melds clever plotting with resourceful camera work, with sympathetic characters that are fascinatingly morbid. South Korean filmmaker Bong Joon-ho follows his monster extravaganza  "The Host" (2006), in firm control of his medium in a different genre, proving once again that conventions need not always confine.

After a night of drinking and waiting for his long time friend, Do-joon (Won Bin), finds himself in some serious trouble. The next morning, he is accused of murdering a young woman on his way home from the bar, and he has no recollection of whether or not he did. The case has enough evidence to be closed quickly, but his mother, played by Kim Hye-ja, refuses to believe that her son could do such a thing. So she pushes forward, not accepting  what the police have pieced together, and starts her own investigation to find the real killer, and free her son.

The film is a labyrinthine and cleverly deceptive, and not in a way we might anticipate. Long after a conventional thriller would have its destination in plain sight, "Mother" is still penetrating our assumptions. There are twists are aplenty, and deductions achieved too easily are simply the result of contrived clues and convenient witness testimony. "Mother" delights in confounding viewer expectations. In fact, just when you think it's over, a couple more developments still remain.

The film progresses with remarkable clarity, while drawing surprise and suspense from unexpected places. It's director Joon-ho Bong's unique style of old and modern approaches to filmmaking  his stylistic and subtle ability to weave this story, and employing a witty use of dark humor throughout is what makes this film so impressive. "Mother" slowly burns its way towards revelations and depths of a character's soul that most dramatic thrillers shy away from.

The most surprising aspect of "Mother" is how differently it begins, and from that, what it becomes. Unique and utterly compelling in its entirety, "Mother" concludes in a manner that solves all (or nearly all) outstanding riddles. "Mother" deftly weaves a story about mother's love into a mystery thriller that will keep you guessing every step of the way. I must say I found this a really great watch! Aside from the many cultural nuances, of which there are many, I found it a riveting tale with some very nice twists. Beautifully shot with a very nice musical score by Byung-woo Lee, I found it easy to follow (despite the inconvenience of subtitles). All the performances were excellent but I must pull out Hye-ja Kim for her tremendous portrayal of this driven woman, a great piece of work! Over all, it A wonderful thriller, unraveled masterfully by a director destined to leave a strong legacy in the Korean cinematic history, with exceptional performance by Hye-ja Kim playing the mother whose protective instincts drive her to extremes. Korean auteur Bong Joon-ho returns with yet another masterful revisionist genre film. He's already tackled the murder-mystery (Memories of Murder) and the monster movie (The Host), now he turns his hand to the thriller. On the face of it, Mother doesn't appear to have much in common with run-of-the mill thrill-rides, but like it's title character, the film can be deceptive. What could be more thrilling than a Mother's desperate (and sometimes morally questionable) journey to prove her son's innocence? Mother is a taut, grounded psychological thriller with a liberal dose of Bong's trademark jet-black comedy. There are numerous heart-pounding moments, but also plenty of quieter, well-placed emotional beats to bring you crashing back down to reality. Bong continues to prove he is a master of character - and the mother (Kim Hye-ja) and mentally ill son Doo-joon (Won Bin) are among his finest creations to date. Kim is simply mesmerising throughout, and while some of the mother's actions are questionable (and others downright evil), you're always on her side - it's a great character.  Another fine film a Korean master. It is a very strange movie. The way the mother is treated makes you wonder how the Koreans treat each other in normal life. It is also a creepy movie, not really a thriller or horror movie, but the movie oozes an atmosphere of gloom and doom. And the ending is surprising. Recommended.

Depois de tantas revisões, a sensação sempre é a mesma: Carros é um clássico atemporal. 398.rich_text:
Terminator Genisys Terminator Genisys Reset the future Science Fiction Action Thriller Alan Taylor Emilia Clarke Jai Courtney Arnold Schwarzenegger Jason Clarke Matt Smith J.K. Simmons Lee Byung-hun Dayo Okeniyi Courtney B. Vance Michael Gladis The year is 2029. John Connor, leader of the resistance continues the war against the machines. At the Los Angeles offensive, John's fears of the unknown future begin to emerge when TECOM spies reveal a new plot by SkyNet that will attack him from both fronts; past and future, and will ultimately change warfare forever. Having heard about the dislike for this film, I was expecting it to be much worse. It's still not a good Terminator movie but, It's just forgettable and unneeded. The decision to mess with the lore around Skynet and have a bratty teenage Sarah Conner is a choice that I don't think works very well. The time travel aspects have gotten really stupid in this movie, half way through the movie, Arnold has to actually explain what is happening and why it all makes sense. It's not Tennent bad but it's gotten very silly.  It's watchable it's just not great and you'd be better off spending your time watching Terminator Zero or the Sarah Conner chronicles. A flawed but interesting blend of franchise fan service, blockbuster popcorn spectacle and general sci fi silliness. As many reviewers have said the opening 15-20 minutes is especially well done. Terminator 1 was a horror thriller. T2 was an action phenomenon. Where the Cameron originals had a clear line of focus, this movie sort of throws all the toys at you for a solid 2 hours of mayhem. Thus this film never quite fully develops its own personality beyond 'fan service blockbuster' but it does everything possible to expand from withing that tight constriction of possibilities. An entertaining mess! Most of what viewers have mentioned in their reviews is true. Terminator 5: Genisys is confusing, convoluted and pointless. Easily the worst Terminator film to date.

I was willing to look past the fact this was a reboot, as opposed to a sequel to Terminator 4: Salvation. All for the purpose of enjoying the film for what it was. But I couldn't even do that, because I couldn't follow what was happening most of the time in the story. So when twists happened, I didn't know what to think of them. The fact it's also rated PG-13, doesn't help things. Terminator 4: Salvation was also rated PG-13, which was an issue there as well, but it was still a good film overall. Terminator 5: Genisys isn't. The only redeeming parts were the CGI and prologue. I have no idea how I missed this one - this is my favorite terminator movie now, with a logical and consistent script, stellar acting (Emilia Clarke is fabulous, it's a shame she left the franchise, and Arnold Schwarzenegger has ample screen time and dials in a splendid performance). I am confused about why this one of all the Terminator sequels apparently didn't do well at the box office, especially because not doing well at the box office apparently applies to the highest grossing movie in the series?

The only thing not perfect about this movie is that the planned sequels were cancelled, and given how much I enjoyed it, I would have loved to see those. Did that "actor", who was supposed to play Kyle Reese, ever recovered from terminal case of imaginary latissimus dorsi?
before the movie, biggest worry was for Sarah who was not Linda - she did ok at least... the rest though... who on earth wrote it (oh yeah i know, people who never understood original and T2), but who put a blind person to do the casting? So why does everyone think this film is bad, it's a pretty good one. Yeah it has its flaws and isn't as good as tue first one, but it still great. watching the movie again years later made me appreciate where thw creator was going with this the only thing is wrong actors playing the roles apart from that its a great movie Complete and total mess. No one even tries to save this awful drivel. Lots of plot holes, bad acting, bad story.
Just avoid. PG-13 rating is the least of Genisys' problems. Making time travel the focus of the story was one of the worst decisions ever made. In a nutshell, It's an awful alternate history of the original film. The CGI is too much, especially in the earlier sequences, and the cast just doesn't have that grounded-in-reality spark that makes the original cast so good. Clarke feels out of place, I don't know why they continue to cast Jai Courtney since he can't act, and Arnold is just too awkwardly old to play the part.

399.title: Kraven the Hunter

metadata.tagline: Villains aren't born. They're made.

399.rich_text:
Kraven the Hunter Kraven the Hunter Villains aren't born. They're made. Action Adventure Thriller J.C. Chandor Aaron Taylor-Johnson Ariana DeBose Fred Hechinger Alessandro Nivola Christopher Abbott Russell Crowe Yuri Kolokolnikov Levi Miller Tom Reed Billy Barratt Kraven Kravinoff's complex relationship with his ruthless gangster father, Nikolai, starts him down a path of vengeance with brutal consequences, motivating him to become not only the greatest hunter in the world, but also one of its most feared. A Clichéd Animal Lover’s "Papa Complex" Trapped in 90s Nostalgia250914 (1.5)Watching "Kraven the Hunter" feels like stepping back into a mediocre 90s action flick—a "cliché bibimbap" that is as predictable as it is artificial. The film centers on Sergei Kravinoff, a "beast-man" with a serious father complex, whose powers are derived from the magical blood of a legendary lion named Zar. While Aaron Taylor-Johnson delivers decent action, the character's intelligence is bafflingly inconsistent; he lives in a highly visible glass greenhouse despite being a wanted killer and tries to recruit Calypso, a high-flying lawyer at a top European firm, to join his "hit list" business. The narrative swings wildly, portraying Kraven as an invincible predator one moment and having him easily outmaneuvered the next, making it impossible to find him truly **** supporting cast is equally problematic. His half-brother, Dmitri (Chameleon), suffers through years of their father Nikolai’s abuse, only to eventually inherit the very mafia empire he supposedly loathed. Russell Crowe’s performance as Nikolai is a collection of cringeworthy Russian stereotypes, portraying a father so obsessed with "being a legend" that he leaves his sons to die in lion attacks. Calypso, despite her background as a professional investigator, is reduced to a mere plot device who exists solely to provide Kraven with magical potions and crossbow support. Even the villains like Rhino and Foreigner are wasted; Foreigner is taken out by a simple crossbow bolt after being built up as a master assassin, and Rhino’s exit is laughably hollow. The film is a string of missed opportunities and jarring directing choices—like the awkward reveal of Kraven’s armory—that prove the SSU (Sony’s Spider-Man Universe) is struggling to find its footing. It’s a series of "Why?" moments that leave the audience feeling no regret as the credits roll, only a sense of fatigue from the repetitive tropes of a bygone era. Feels like it was written for very young viewers. The CGI is poor, the dialogue is genuinely bad, and while the main actor does a solid job, much of the supporting acting is painfully weak. The story tries to sell twists, but none of them land or feel surprising, which makes the whole plot feel flat and predictable.There are a few redeeming moments. Like with all horror movies, there are some problems that the protagonists need to solve or overcome in some way.

In this case, the protagonists live their lives while making minimal noise to alert the creatures which hunt by sound.

While I have some complaints about how the characters sometimes make stupid decisions this is common in horror movies.

Overall I loved this movie! You're silent or you're dead in this unique twist on the post-apocalypse. Stalked by blind, stick-like predators with unnaturally precise hearing, a small family struggles to carry on and make a life for themselves in an abandoned farm house.

Seems like it's tough to find genuinely new, original concepts in genre film these days, but A Quiet Place certainly fits the bill. We've grown so accustomed to big bangs and fiery finales on the silver screen that ninety minutes of quiet stillness feels like a completely foreign experience. The near-total silence is efficiently played for dramatic tension, poked and prodded in inventive ways that demonstrate the lengths this family has gone to maintain normalcy (exterior doors left permanently open, sand-lined paths through the most commonly used walkways) and, occasionally, broken in a few moments of pure, unguarded terror.

As gimmicks go, it's a particularly effective one, though the plot is often forced into contrived scenarios to connect its various ideas and to artificially generate extra layers of suspense. It's one of those movies where you'll facepalm over boneheaded decisions and wonder aloud how these people managed to survive for so long. In other words, it manages to both buck horror stereotypes and embrace them. The potential was there to be much better. a unique movie in how little dialogue there is which I think helps showcase the horror of the situation When A Quiet Place first hit theaters in 2018, the astonishing story was easy to follow and easily entertaining. Most viewers would like to think of it as another generic thriller movie. I like to think about it as a heartfelt one-of-a-kind movie, one that needed a lot of thought and effort. Still good tho but has the least rewatch ability Film that introduces the main story of the saga on which the stories told in the next chapters will be based. The plot has a rather classic development, with a good dose of action and adrenaline but with some elements that characterize the main story that enter in a forced and banal way in some cases More of the same, but still a good movie overall. Alot of cool action scenes of martial art fighting & shoot outs with neat twists in the story. Sadece vur kır tam olarak bana hitap etmiyor, eksik kalıyor benim için. Ortalama ve altı bir yapım bence. Quite a lot of times, you see the second movie of a franchise not live up to the same standards as the first but John Wick 2 definitely did. You could argue that it was better than the first. Great movie all round. The rare case of a really good sequel. It has everything what made the original movie so entertaining and adds more action. lore, worldbuilding and new characters. After rounding up the loose ends of the last movie John Wick wants to go back into retirement. However he had drawn a lot of attention towards him so a former associate wants to collect a debt from John and he cant refuse without dire consequences. This is the set up for the story. I was surprised that they made a sequel I would rate even higher than the first movie. It is immersive, hugely entertaining, has style and superb focus even on details. There is no boring scene, all sets look amazing and the characters were perfectly chosen. Keanu Reeve, Ian McShane, Lance **** and John Leguizamo return to their roles and fully deliver. They nail their roles and I want to see more of them. The new characters are equally strong. Ricardo Scarmarcio, Ruby Rose, Laurence Fishburne and Common (Lonnie Rashid Lynn) are so entertaining to watch. The action scenes are superb and the franchise is the poster child for the term Gun Fu. Nearly no (modern) movie makes you feel the impact and intensity like this. As example: Many movies are visually too dark and have shaky cameras during action scenes. Here they are fixated that you can clearly see whats going on. Lastly it has an incredible set up for a sequel. Overall this is for me slightly better than the original. Me and my friends were entertained from beginning to the end. Its a 10/10 for me. Absolutely adored this movie more than the first. The story is plain and simple like the first but there are some Absolutely brilliant scenes throughout the movie. Specifically the art gallery at the end is amazingly done. 

Just like the first movie there is no sparing in this movie. John sets out to kill, and kill he does. 

Overall this adds more depth to the John Wick universe and Im all here for it The movie is an improvement over the first one. The story, while still predictable to an extend, is much more complex than the first, and intriguing. It has a great amount of build-up leading to the climax. The ending of this film was a downside for me, as I didn't expect it to end on a cliffhanger; it felt like an anticlimax and I craved for more. The movie also remains fairly dull in the first 15-25 minutes, just like the first film which is another downside. Overall, it's a solid action thriller, and you should definitely watch this one!

416.title: Aquaman

metadata.tagline: Home is calling.

416.rich_text:
Aquaman Aquaman Home is calling. Action Adventure Fantasy James Wan Jason Momoa Amber Heard Willem Dafoe Patrick Wilson Nicole Kidman Dolph Lundgren Yahya Abdul-Mateen II Temuera Morrison Ludi Lin Michael Beach Half-human, half-Atlantean Arthur Curry is taken on the journey of his lifetime to discover if he is worth of being a king. Genellikle DC evrenini ve filmlerini sevmem ama bu sefer fena değildi. Süper kahraman filmi yerine blade tarzı karanlık bir evrende geçse daha iyi olabilirdi... It always baffled me how this film made over a billion dollars at the box office. It's stunning to look at, but it isn't really anything new. The most MCU film of the DCEU at the point of release might have contributed to it's success. The film starts well and then falls into banality and a plot seen and reviewed over and over again for this genre. The length of the film is also excessive for what it has to tell Happy 7 year anniversary Aquaman review one of my favorite dc superhero character full action pack fight scenes amazing storyline amazing visuals with 4k ultra high definition high dynamic range10 Dolby vision and Dolby atoms with amazing sound systems for it made it better saw it twice in the movie theaters so happy Aquman made 1.152 billion dollars at the box office 5 star 10 out 10 star 100 out 100 star I felt it really knew how to bring and combine the 2 worlds Earth and Atlantis together to bring a solid start to the Aquaman era. I really thought this movie really did swim the ludacrist excitement as I found Aquaman really badass and robotic. The son of a humble lighthouse keeper (The Book of Boba Fett's Temuera Morrison) and an exiled queen of Atlantis (Nicole Kidman) spends his entire childhood honing a set of innate underwater capabilities. He then grows up to single-handedly avert maritime disasters, foil modern-day pirates and pal around with the Justice League.

It's Jason Momoa, of course, in a fascinating bit of casting that's worked out very well despite (or, perhaps, because of) his total dissimilarity from the classic character's original design. Aquaman probably *should* look different from the rest of the JLA, and in addition to his Polynesian appearance, Momoa sports a natural grace and fluidity in the water that pairs well with his brute physicality. Not everyone can look smooth and cool while hefting a nuclear submarine from the ocean depths, but this guy makes it a dynamic spectacle.

That's where this standalone Aquaman vehicle shines: inserting its star into spectacular poster-friendly moments, pumping up the jams and capitalizing on the easy returns. Those action scenes succeed where most of the story doesn't. The plot, a disjointed mix of political maneuvers, vengeful sons and mythic treasures, is a wishy-washy mess that stumbles and bumbles from one predictable turn to the next. It's exposition central, a cavalcade of breathless details, but still manages to leave dozens of gaping logic holes untended. There's no flicker between Momoa and his female counterpart, a stiff-lipped Amber Heard, so their romantic connection feels sudden and empty. Even Willem Dafoe struggles to make anything of a rather large supporting role, saddled as he is by bad dialogue and a bland character arc.

I enjoyed the big and loud and shiny bits, appreciated the vision of a science fiction story where all the dazzling technological advances have taken place beneath the waves, rather than overhead in the stars, but couldn't overlook the flimsy fabric holding it all together. There’s something here; we just can’t quite see it yet. I've tried several times to get through this movie with no luck. I fall asleep. Jason Momoa is uninteresting in everything, but in this, he is extremely uninteresting. 2018년 당시 디씨의 구원자. 인물 비주얼도 좋고 영상미도 좋다. 특히 메라가 인어공주 그자체. 잠수씬에서 공포영화같은 연출도 너무 좋았다. 옴이랑 블랙만타 비주얼도 좋았는데 비중조절은 약간 실패한듯 Погружающий визуал, грациозные перетекания меж планами, а также плавная смена настроенческого русла. Единственное, что «топит» картину, так это нехватка большей сюжетной глубины. В остальном же — отличный (в)водный фильм о морском герое без какой-либо сценарной «воды». I fell asleep in the cinema. It was like a Power Rangers movie, so boring. Black Manta looks like a power rangers villain. Horrible movie.

417.title: Soul

metadata.tagline: Everybody has a soul. Joe Gardner is about to find his.

417.rich_text:
Soul Soul Everybody has a soul. Joe Gardner is about to find his. Animation Family Comedy Fantasy Drama Music Pete Docter Jamie Foxx Tina Fey Graham Norton Rachel House Alice Braga Richard Ayoade Phylicia Rashād Donnell Rawlings Questlove Angela Bassett Joe Gardner is a middle school teacher with a love for jazz music. After a successful audition at the Half Note Club, he suddenly gets into an accident that separates his soul from his body and is transported to the You Seminar, a center in which souls develop and gain passions before being transported to a newborn child. Joe must enlist help from the other souls-in-training, like 22, a soul who has spent eons in the You Seminar, in order to get back to Earth. 나를 포함한 많은 사람들은 생각한다."언젠가 나는 꿈을 이룰거야. 지금은 그냥 그 순간을 위해 버티는거야."하지만 속으로는 알고있다. 꿈은 만들어나가려 달리지 않는 한 그저 공상일 뿐임을. 사실 닿을 수 없는 곳에 놓여 있어서 그 자체로 우리를 안도하게 하는 핑계일 뿐이라는 것을."I will live every minute."살아나갈 용기없는 비겁한 우리도 그럴 수 있기를...201227 (4.0)-1. 픽사 식 디즈니 인트로는 이런건가 ㅋㅋㅋ 뿡빵거리는 그루브 조오타!2. 영혼 중 한국 여자애가 갑툭튘 ㅋㅋ 귀여워3. ”My life was meaningless" 이 얼마나 두려운 말인가4. 우울감, 자괴감에 빠져 자신을 잊은 이들을 구해내는 것은 명상가들. 이런 컨셉 좋다. 영혼의 세계에 와서 구출하러 다니는거야 자신을 구하는 명상인줄 알았지만 타인을 구하는!5. 빠져들어서 의식을 놓고 집중하는 사람들의 영혼이 모이는 zone이 나오는 게 좋았다. 우리모두 그런 경험있잖아 내가 어디서 뭘 하는지 모를만큼 빠져드는 순간이.6. 그리고 즐거워서 빠져드는 것과 압박감에 자신을 잃는 게 한끝차이라는 묘사도 좋다.7. You 세미나 운영하는 제리 의 멀대잖아ㅋㅋㅋㅋㅋㅋ8. spark는 재능이라고만 생각했는데, 22번의 spark는 '감사' 였던 것 같다. 그래서 그 어떤 관계도 맺을 수 없는 Great Before 에서는 아무것도 느끼지 못한 것. 22번이면 아주 초창기 영혼인데 그 오랜 세월동안 말이다. 항상 뭔가 특별한 목표에 대한 성취가 있을거라 미뤄왔던 조는 꿈을 이루고도 여전히 컴컴하고 외로운 자신의 집을 들여다보며 깨닫는다. 22번이 남기고 간 '삶 자체에 대한 감사'를...9. 22번을 떠올리며 조가 연주하는 음악에 눈물이 막 솟았다. 아무 대사가 없어도 뭘 말하고 싶은지 너무나 알 것 같았다.10. 역시 티나 페이의 목소리는 참 사랑스럽다. Soul has great visuals and direction, but what is most important about this film is its message to its viewers. This film serves to be an exhibit of the grander questions and ideas people have about our origins and the meaning of our existence. It does this excellently but at the cost of simplifying these ideas for the Disney audience. Out of all of Disney's films, I believe this film suffers the most from the "Disneyfication" effect. That is when Disney takes broad and complex concepts and simplifies them to be easily understood and entertaining to its audience. They usually do this by personifying literally every possible subject matter in the film, and giving them human personalities, characteristics and traits they would never  have otherwise.

For example, the Great Before being a fun happy summer camp like place is incredibly corny. Nobody is born with an inherent desire to do anything with their lives. It takes lived experience to find something we love in this world. Although they do depict the main character going through a lot of rejection before he can find his happiness, his love for music is implied to be given to him in life, instead of a desire that emerges based on his decisions in life or the influences around him or the parenting that raised him or any of the many other factors that influence the way we think. There are people in this world that will never find a passion in this world. There are people who's lives are laid out for them by their family, but still go completely off their path. Saying that everything you are in life is because you were given it untrue to many people's actual life. Ideas like that cheapen human experience for the sake of making cute films that children will cherish without any complicated truths.

The Disneyfication of this film's direction aside, it is excellent in an incredible amount of ways. Its art and animation is incredibly detailed and vivid. It most likely used computers and software to create the models and animation instead of by hand, but the result is an incredibly compelling visual art piece. Even with its simplistic storytelling, at the core of this film is a profound message with heartfelt intentions that leave you with a sense of wonder. Its characters are full of personality that could be developed further than what we see in the film, which is a result of the depth of the films writing. And of course, grand ideas combined with Disney's ability for filmmaking creates a special quality of film that isn't quantifiable. I think they call it Disney magic.

Overall this film is great. If you can look past its corny messaging you'll see something special. Una gran película, de las mayormente maduras de Pixar, una formula y dinámica común pero explorada de una muy buena manera. Filme maravilhoso que fala do sentido da vida.

Nota 10 para a originalidade, é um dos filmes mais originais que já vi.

Até o começo é surpreendente que quando o Joel (personagem principal) vai finalmente realizar seu sonho de ser musico famoso, ele morre do nada por não olhar por onde anda, enebreado na felicidade e vai parar no pós-vida onde deveria reencarnar mas ele foge pro jardim do pré-vida numa cena incrível de originalidade, onde é mostrado as almas daqueles que ainda não viverem se formando, ele acaba sendo confudido com um Dr. Notável e vira um tutor de uma dessas almas, a n° 22 que é bem carismatica. Juntos eles tentam procurar o sentido de vida e acabam fugindo pra terra onde ela entra no corpo dele e ele no de um gato.

Essa metade do filme achei a mais fraca mas mesmo assim é legal, vai mostrando o Joel tentado fazer a 22 realizar seu sonho de ser musico enquanto mostra ela aprendendo sobre tudo. Não é uma parte ruim, é gostoso de ver algumas partes mas outras fica cansativo. Depois Joel recupera seu corpo, vira músico mas acha que esse não é o proposito da vida dele (diferente do que ele achava) e 22 vai pro além mas vira uma alma perdida.

Joel volta pro além e salva ela e ela finalmente vai pra terra, enquanto as criaturas do além decidem dar outra chance do Joel viver. Apesar desse final ser cliche ele é bem feito. Detalhe pra cena do Terry (semi-vilão louco por contar) que é enganado quando um ser do além fala: "olha pra lá que absurdo" e bota pro lado uma pedra do ábaco dele, o enganado. "Soul" é um filme belíssimo, com uma premissa fascinante e uma execução visual impecável. No entanto, sua mensagem pode parecer um pouco confusa, e seu ritmo oscila entre momentos brilhantes e trechos arrastados. Ainda assim, é uma animação que vale a pena assistir, especialmente para quem gosta de reflexões sobre a vida e a arte.Nota: 9.0/10 – Ótimo Pixar toys with jazz and the afterlife in this quirky, blissful rumination on the nature of inspiration and the meaning of life. The film's superficial framework involves an optimistic high school music teacher, trapped in a body-swap triangle with a wary spirit and an emotional therapy cat, but it's really all about a sweeping sense of discovery, about celebrating the miracle of consciousness and the little daily pleasures we all take for granted.

In-between crisp, validating episodes on a lovely day in autumnal NYC, we also play with a heap of peculiar, interesting ground rules and unusual conundrums on an odd, colorful alternate plane of being. This gives the creative team both the time and liberty to really go for it, a chance to portray all manner of abstract visual concepts in their own distinctive fashion and, to the surprise of none, I'm sure, they're an unparalleled success. A theoretical masterpiece in motion. Those scenes, plus the equally hypnotic musical breaks when our narrator sits down behind a piano and lets the moment sweep him away, had me wrapped up from the first hit.

No surprise this is from the same director who brought us Monsters Inc., Up and Inside Out: it's a perfect spiritual successor to that powerful string of rich, emotive, conceptual heavyweights. Come for the wacky comic situations, the top-notch voice acting (Jamie Foxx and Tina Fey fit together like a jigsaw puzzle) and the flashy renderings (Pixar's visual team has leveled-up yet again), stay for the life lessons and mind-easing philosophical notes. A groovy, stimulating, feel-good wonder. May just be the best animated film I have ever seen. Definitely have good points for serious audience. Excellent de A à Z, personnages très attachants, doublage français aux **** oignons mais le point fort du film reste sa déconstruction brutale et élégante qui sert de transition d'un sujet à un autre + animation ultra fluide et clean + trop bien + ratio You never know where "Soul" is going.  It's full of surprises.  However, on the way to getting there, we get to enjoy some of the best animation ever.  The mixture of colors is breathtaking.  There are a couple of stretches that drag, but overall, this was easily the best animation movie of 2020.  It's too bad the pandemic took a bite out of the box office.  I would have loved to have seen how an animated film with predominantly black characters would have fared. La premisa es muy sencilla: Joe Gardner no quiere viajar al mundo de los muertos y se ve sumido en un viaje con 22, un espíritu que no quiere ir a la Tierra. Parece poca cosa, pero estamos hablando de que esta película rompe todos los esquemas de las películas de Pixar: nos habla del mejor modo de vivir la vida, de lo que nos mueve (la llamada chispa en la cinta) y, sorprendentemente, del más allá. No me esperaba algo tan atrevido y tan sublime por parte de Pixar hoy en día,  pero me han demostrado que pueden seguir haciendo películas que saquen lágrimas y que enseñen lecciones de vida a pequeños y mayores por igual. La recomiendo a todo público; llegando a decir que Soul es una de las mejores películas del estudio. Con un final que estoy seguro que impactará a más de una, una historia de desmotivación del protagonista que muchos identificarán como suya y momentos que te dejarán con la sensación de estar dentro del largometraje, creo que mi calificación es más que merecida.

418.title: Midsommar

Midsommar Midsommar Let the festivities begin. The cinematography and production is excellent, and creates a uniquely unsettling mood. That said, its unnecessarily protracted duration is tedious. For me, at its best Midsommer is uniquely enjoyable in the moment, but probably won't have much long-term resonance. I doubt I'll be inclined to view it again. Pleno verano

The movie's rating is significantly deflated by the fact that it advertises itself as a horror movie, but it just isn't. It attracts horror fans, but the correct target audience are people who like thought-provoking movies and aren't immediately turned off by atrocity and moral ambiguity. If that's the target audience that the movie tried to appeal towards, it would have a much higher rating.

But judging the movie for what it is, it's one the most immersive and thought-provoking movies I've seen in a long time. It really made me think very deeply about the topics of excessive individualism in the West; the idea that death is a lot less scary in the presence of a community or transcendent order that one sees as an extension of oneself, and which outlives oneself; the sense of profound meaning and belonging that can arise from a rich shared culture; but at the same time the absolute atrocities at the individual level that can be overlooked or even embraced with an excessive focus on community; the lack of ultimate purpose and unique contribution when every generation is an exact copy of the last; and the absolute hellscape and moral bankruptcy that can ensue from getting too comfortable with the ideas of death and suffering.

I cannot understate how much the movie made me think about these topics. I'm not exaggerating when I say that this movie influenced my worldview. Not directly - as it doesn't intend to give all the answers - but it certainly intends to ask questions, which it does with incredible efficiency, in my opinion.

In addition to its thought-provoking nature, it also uses horror, ambiguity, and the striking unfamiliarity of the cult to the protagonists to create a sense of mystery, which makes the movie very immersive, in my opinion. 

All in all, I genuinely think it's pretty close to a masterpiece. It's certainly not going to be too everyone's taste, and it has its fair share of repulsive scenes, but those whom the movie is for are going to get a LOT out of the movie, I think. Wonka Wonka Every good thing in this world started with a dream. Comedy Family Fantasy Paul King Timothée Chalamet Calah Lane Keegan-Michael Key Hugh Grant Paterson Joseph Olivia Colman Tom Davis Jim Carter Rowan Atkinson Matt Lucas Willy Wonka – chock-full of ideas and determined to change the world one delectable bite at a time – is proof that the best things in life begin with a dream, and if you’re lucky enough to meet Willy Wonka, anything is possible. timothée chalamet es de los mejores actores y por esta peli conocia todo, como dune, marty suprime, Call Me by Your Name obras de arte The first thing that stands out is that it works without making too much noise. It doesn’t try to justify its existence every minute or compete head-on with the memories we already have of the character. It goes another way, with a fairly conscious lightness, and that’s appreciated. It lets itself be watched with a constant smile, unhurried, without needing to prove that it’s smarter or deeper than it really wants to **** film is entertaining almost from the start, with a rhythm that doesn’t weigh it down and humor that goes down easily. Not everything lands equally well, but it rarely stalls. There’s a sense of a well-oiled spectacle, of a carefully made product, where each piece knows its role. It doesn’t dazzle through ambition, but through craft, and these days that’s no small thing.Visually it’s very well worked. The production design has charm, color, and detail, without fully tipping into overload. At times it seems like it might become cloying, but it usually pulls back just in time. The staging has something classical about it, almost like a musical from another era, and that choice strongly defines the overall tone: it’s a film that isn’t afraid at all of being kind.Timothée Chalamet holds the whole together with a performance that doesn’t try to imitate or compete with anyone. He doesn’t always have the magnetism needed to lift certain scenes, but he does have a steady presence that keeps the story standing. It works better when he lowers the intensity and lets the character breathe, rather than when he pushes the exuberance.Where it falters a bit is in the sense of necessity. It feels like the story moves forward more by inertia than by true narrative urgency. It doesn’t bother, but it also doesn’t leave a deep mark. It’s one of those films you enjoy while it lasts and remember fondly… though without the feeling of having seen something **** in all, it’s a likable, well-made proposal that’s honest about what it wants to offer. It doesn’t reinvent anything, nor does it need to. At times it’s charming, at times a bit predictable, but always pleasant. A decent sweet, perhaps not memorable, but very easy to consume. This movie was AMAZING!!! I love this movie, the soundtrack is still amazing even in 2025, Warner Bros. Give yourself a pat on the back because this is better then any Disney musical, or any musical in general, 10/10!!! Timothee Chalamet does a great job at portraying Willy Wonka, as not only does he capture the "magic" of Wonka, but he's also able to follow through with the various songs that the movie offers. The movie is sure to capture the hearts of people of all ages. Achei o início lento, muito lento, musical demais...e Deus do **** filme enrolado.

"Beetlejuice Beetlejuice (2024)" brings back the chaotic and beloved bio-exorcist in a fun, visually impressive sequel that leans heavily on nostalgia. Tim Burton's signature style is all over the film, from the dark humor to the quirky, gothic worldbuilding that fans loved in the original.Michael Keaton returns as the titular character, and his performance is as energetic and mischievous as ever, reminding audiences why Beetlejuice remains one of his most iconic roles. The supporting cast, including some new faces, add fresh dynamics to the story, but they often feel overshadowed by Keaton's larger-than-life **** film's strength lies in its commitment to the eccentric and bizarre, with impressive practical effects and imaginative set pieces. However, the story lacks the sharp wit and cleverness of its predecessor. The plot feels a bit uneven at times, and some of the jokes don't land as well, leaving the movie reliant on visual spectacle rather than substance.Overall, "Beetlejuice Beetlejuice" is an enjoyable watch for fans of the original, offering enough nostalgia and chaos to entertain. Yet, it doesn't fully capture the magic of the 1988 classic, making it a fun but slightly underwhelming follow-up. Beetlejuice Beetlejuice. It's back! Not really. #TheShortHandCritic: Just when all hope seemed lost—the sequel to #Beetlejuice is resurrected from the grave. #BeetlejuiceBeetlejuice finds the Deetz family selling off their iconic white house when the patriarch of the family has passed. Lydia (#WinonaRyder) begins to sense that her childhood demon (whose name we shall not speak) is tormenting her from the afterlife again. Her daughter Astrid (#JennaOrtega) doesn’t believe in her mother’s abilities—however Beetlejuice is about to make a believer out of her. Ortega plays her character with the same spoiled **** that many of her roles have required of her. It’s rather tiresome at times. #CatherineOhara has her moments, but her performance feels like a subset of #SchittsCreek. #MichaelKeaton is on fire again as the wild and irresistible title character. However, this time the movie belongs to Ryder who reminds us of that kooky old school charm that the Ortega-generation just simply can’t seem to match. There’s unexpected dimension in Lydia proving Ryder is still a terrific actress. Charlie and the Chocolate Factory (2005)

Delicious Adventure

(11,957 – 25 Nov 2005 / 02 Oct 2025 – by Claudio Carvalho)

The eccentric manufacturer of chocolates and candies Willy Wonka (Johnny Depp) closes his factory due to industrial espionage. Many years later, he reopens and promotes a tour through his factory, the greatest in the world, through five golden tickets hidden in the bars of chocolate. The poor and sweet boy Charlie Bucket (Freddie Highmore) finds one, for the pride and joy of his very supportive family. He spends the day in a mysterious competition for an unknown award with four other nasty boys and girls. Who will win the prize?

"Charlie and the Chocolate Factory" is a delightful and delicious adventure through the world of fantasy. Tim Burton changes his usual morbid scenarios to very bright ones, and keeps the usual weird character, magnificently performed by the awesome Johnny Depp. This movie is highly recommended for the whole family, and it is excellent entertainment. Unfortunately, I have not had the chance to watch the original 1971 "Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory" to make a comparison, but this remake is really a great movie. My vote is eight.

actors are perfectly casted and story is strange but really creative A "A Fantástica Fábrica de Chocolate" é um clássico da literatura infantil que foi adaptado para o cinema em duas ocasiões. A primeira versão cinematográfica foi lançada em 1971, sob o título "Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory", dirigida por Mel Stuart, que pra mim continua imbatível, mágica, muito mais equilibrada com a vida do garoto pobre Charlie que consegue ter a oportunidade de conhecer a famosa fábrica de chocolate.

Esta segunda versão, intitulada "A Fantástica Fábrica de Chocolate", foi lançada em 2005 e dirigida por Tim Burton. Ambas as versões do filme são baseadas no livro "Charlie e a Fábrica de Chocolate", escrito por Roald Dahl. O Wonka interpretado por Gene Wilder na versão de 1971 é muito mais assustador e ambíguo do que o Wonka interpretado por Johnny Depp nesta versão de 2005, o qual usa de todos seus cacoetes e maneirismo para criar um excêntrico chocolatier.

Definitivamente não gosto do Depp, sempre acima do tom. No entanto, para a sorte dele (e nossa) a excentricidade combinou muito aqui, pela atmosfera que Tim Burton sabe muito bem conduzir.

A trama então vai girar em torno das cinco crianças sortudas que encontram bilhetes dourados em suas barras de chocolate. A fábrica é um lugar mágico, cheio de maravilhas e delícias, mas também está repleta de desafios e lições morais para as crianças. Cada uma das crianças selecionadas para a visita tem características distintas e enfrenta consequências específicas relacionadas aos seus comportamentos, e com a ajuda dos Oopa-Loompa (os trabalhadores esquisitos da fábrica), o roteiro vai dando seu recado.

É incrível como a caracterização dos oompa-loopmpas e as músicas do primeiro são bem melhor construída, confesso que fiquei desapontado aqui, as músicas são terríveis, soaram genéricas, usando a cada parição um ritmo diferente, mas o que é pior, sem o carisma tão característicos das criaturas.

A história é conhecida por sua imaginação extravagante, humor peculiar e, às vezes, por seu tom moralizador. Ela destaca a importância de valores como honestidade, moderação e respeito pelos outros. Mas aqui, algo que mexeu um pouco comigo foi a ênfase demasiada no Wonka, talvez por termos um Depp lhe conferindo vida. Assim, o filme instrumentaliza o Charlie, sendo o conflito principal a relação familiar do Wonka. Ok, fez sentido, mas confesso que mexeu com meus sentimento nostálgico.

De resto, Tim Burton continua visualmente agradável e extravagante, a fábrica tem seu toque artístico e peculiar, o que é bem bonito e interessante. "A Fantástica Fábrica de Chocolate" tornou-se um clássico atemporal, e vejo que ambas as versões são apreciadas por diferentes gerações. Growing up with the Johnny Depp version, Charlie And The Chocolate Factory was definitely a nostalgic movie for me, it's part of my childhood and so it's always perfect every time i watch it, the performance, the song, the set, and the story was timeless, rewatching it for like a thousand times just recently and it's still really good. Compared to the 1971 version, Tim Burton's rendition has an overall tone that is more whimsical, peculiar, and dark. Johnny Depp injects Willy Wonka with more personal flair, and the adaptation of the story gives the entire work a different and refreshing flavour. Most creepy Willy Wonka ever.

В фильме вообще в общей сложности снимается всего пять актёров! Удивительно, да? Horror Ben Leonberg Indy Shane Jensen Arielle Friedman Larry Fessenden Stuart Rudin Anya Krawcheck Hunter Goetz Bandit A loyal dog moves to a rural family home with his owner Todd, only to discover supernatural forces lurking in the shadows. As dark entities threaten his human companion, the brave pup must fight to protect the one he loves most. 'Good Boy' never fully exploits its twisted premise of watching a man in a dog suit act like one all the time. The film addresses certain current problems focused on human relationships, mainly the supposed connection that social networks bring and the destructive emotional ties people build. Unfortunately, the film soon uses all kinds of conveniences to advance the story, causing more unintentional comedy than intrigue or terror. Furthermore, the main plot twist, in hindsight, isn't that interesting when you realize that it was the only possible route to propel the story. Although the film delivers some discomfort to be attractive, the promise of something more disturbing is only materialized in the last sequence, where the darkest aspects of human beings are finally revealed. The usual pedo critics will appreciate this mediocre soft porn thriller, but as true ratings (user) indicates, this is a waste of time.

The story involves the theft and recovery of a priceless Renaissance painting, the battle for an enormous family fortune and the slow and then sudden upheavals that transformed Europe during the first half of the 20th century. The Grand Budapest Hotel delivers the unique style and deadpan humour audiences have come to expect from Wes Anderson and this story of a hotel concierge set against a background of war torn Europe (albeit a fictional approximation) is arguable his best movie to date. At times unwatchable The Grand Budapest Hotel marks the point in Anderson's body of work where his artificial worldview culminates with a warmth that he’s often, unfairly, accused of lacking. In other words, in this film, Anderson perfects his camerawork, his interplay with set design and color palettes, and his choice of actors.

️ The fairy-tale setting is ideal for a crime comedy featuring an unresolved murder, numerous suspects, and quirky characters. The tone remains humorous throughout, though the absurdity of events is tempered by well-placed moments of empathy.

️ It's an absolute delight from start to finish—a film like a treasure chest that beams its contents at the audience. Occasionally, however, when political events start to take center stage, unsettling parallels to the present day emerge, and the laughter catches in your throat for a moment. At this point I think we're pretty much beyond hope that Wes Anderson will ever try a different style of filmmaking, and for that I wish more power to him. Even the stop-motion children's film The Fantastic Mr. Fox, despite its literary origins, is indisputably Anderson from start to finish. So, in lieu of a proper evolution, perhaps the best one can hope for is for Mr. Anderson to make the perfect Wes Anderson movie. The Grand Budapest Hotel falls quite close to that ideal.

Thoroughly quirky, lovingly composed with a strict eye for heavy detail, funny and dense and sweet and genuine, it's everything I love about his pictures, **** over the skeleton of a different tale. The man certainly has his favorites - recurring actors from earlier in his career appear in the dozens throughout this one - but you'll smile and applaud their arrival, one by one, like traveling players in a variety of elaborate costumes and characters.

Ralph Fiennes is magnificent as the leading man, a silky-smooth, primped, proper, profane concierge with a knack for elderly women and a ferocious wit. His understudy, lobby boy Anthony Quiñonez, is the film's anchor: a particularly straight, self-assured young lead who's cut from the same cloth as Rushmore's Max Fischer. Richly funny, otherworldy in its beauty, quick and sharp as a tack, it goes a bit overboard in the third act but that's all in the name of good fun.
