Predators (2010) is a surprisingly underrated and now peak installment in the Predator franchise. While Prey and Badlands are rightly praised, Predators deserves far more love as well . It was one of the earliest true legacy sequels, paying clear homage to the 1987 original while confidently expanding the **** film’s emphasis on survival is one of its greatest strengths. Royce and Isabelle are among the better-developed protagonists in the franchise, and their slow-burn trust feels earned. The Crucified Predator being positioned as a reluctant “good guy” was a standout choice, especially when he faces off against the Berserker Super-Predator. Their conflict feels like a Shakespearean blood feud, adding thematic weight beyond simple monster **** Predators’ presence is felt even when they’re off-screen, reinforcing the tension and the idea that these are dishonorable hunters, breaking the traditional code we associate with the species. Contrary to some criticism, I actually liked the Super Predators, and the Berserker needing help from a Classic Jungle Hunter — and ultimately Royce — made his defeat more satisfying. Royce delivering the killing blow felt symbolic, marking the rise of a new legacy ****, the film has flaws. The cliffhanger ending doesn’t fully land, and the pacing can be uneven. But in retrospect, Predators feels very much like a shadow-directed Robert Rodriguez project, similar to how Tom Cruise steers the Mission: Impossible films — and that’s not a bad thing.Originally dismissed as mediocre upon release, Predators has aged extremely well and now stands proudly alongside newer installments and the 1987 original.

Great Music By John Debney(The Mummy Tomb Of The Dragon Emperor) & Themes by Alan Sliverstri (Predator) , Cinematography   By Gyula Pados(The Duchess) , Produced By Robert Rodriguez(Planet Terror)  and Direction By Nimrod Antal(Armored). Predators (2010): The Underrated Legacy Sequel That Aged Into a Classic 8.1/10 Predators is a slightly above-average movie that’s enjoyable but tough to review. It doesn’t do anything radical—mostly a meandering rehash of the original—but introduces unique ideas alongside ones that seed the franchise’s downfall later. In isolation, it’s a missed opportunity with untapped potential. Overall, don’t hate it, had fun—but wasted potential. The first time I saw this movie in theaters, I left completely disappointed. I was younger back then and realized that the film tries to honor the original, but ends up feeling like a weak copy rather than a proper tribute to the first classic. I’d recommend watching it on a rainy Sunday if you have nothing else to **** my ranking, it comes fourth after Predator, Predator 2, and Prey. That doesn’t mean it’s a movie I wouldn’t recommend — if you like Predator, many people have enjoyed this film. I give it a 6 because there are some moments that make the movie shine, though I won’t specify which **** ending, in my opinion, is a disaster. I don’t consider it a bad movie, but it was a big disappointment, and even though I can watch it occasionally, I can’t give it a higher score. In my opinion, it’s overrated, especially compared to Predator 2, which is brilliant and underrated. A very good new installment in the predator franchise with a unique situation 8/10 a good new  installment with great action sequences I'm good audience for anything with Brody, but he's used at 5% capacity here. Sure, he makes a more believable modern elite soldier than da old bodybuilders. The movie bears some ressemblance to McTiernan's Predator, but without the knowhow. I mean Predator showed the characters a bit, then some action against guerilleros and russians, then they were picked one by one in epic ways. Schwarzie stumbles by luck into some mud camouflaging him from the Predator. I suppose it's the special kind used to make ceramics, not just some garden dirt. Js.. here Brody just muds himself for no reason. Characters are dropped just supposing they're good, no action showing their skills, then they get slaughtered. Plus the doctor... how is a psycho good prey again.. he only knows how to kill defenseless people... And a guy in a wreck hiding from Predators for years.. gets killed 10secs later. Not to mention the implications of this setup.. so what they have billions of cams all over the galaxy then some low-wage Predators watch that cr@p to pick targets and abduct them ? Wow.. it's just nonsensical (and fairly stupid) all along. Only last 30mins are of some interest Predators returns to familiar themes of jungle and hunting, evoking the sweltering heat of an '80s summer. While this strong sense of familiarity might be seen as lacking innovation, considering the trajectory of the Predator franchise, returning to its roots isn't necessarily a bad thing. Il paraît que ce bon vieux Predator (le vrai, le seul, l’unique de 1987) s’est fait hara-kiri en voyant cet étron ! comme on le comprend ! c’est ici une infâme série Z dont le pseudo-scénario a été écrit sur une vieux post-it qui ne collait plus depuis longtemps. 

Ce misérable bousin est en effet aussi palpitant qu’un épisode entier de Derrick. Les « Aliens vs Predator » étaient déjà des dérivés dégénérés de la célèbre licence mais là, on touche le fond ! 

Quant à Adrien Brody, il fait ce qu’il peut mais il est entouré de comédiens de seconde zone qui pataugent dans ce cloaque de nanar ni fait ni à faire. Aberrant et bâclé, ramolli du bulbe et pas crédible pour un dollar, ce film de merde est complètement à côté de la plaque ! What i felt in the movie for it's entirely until the last 30 minutes of the film was the same feeling that i have with the original 1987 Predator with Arnold Schwarzenegger, which is a movie that i thought wasn't bad overall but i wouldn't say i like it, there is some good interesting stuff in it but there is also some uninteresting stuff in it that could sometimes be whatever and ok but also could be pretty flawed, but for mostly i just felt that it was a ok enough film for me to still engaged with the story and with these flawed characters, until like i mention earlier the last 30 minutes which i think was the best part of the movie and i can say that it was a good last 30 minutes, and so i gave another half of point for that, overall Predators was another flawed attempt in a franchise that somehow i never really bothered, but mostly it wasn't something that just plain terrible stuff (except for the god awful Predator 2), same thing happen here, it was an ok film with enough passable stuff, and in my opinion the best solo Predator movie so far. Great effects, but my biggest problem is that the characters are so shallow at points you want the predators to kill them. Predators is a bit of a pleasant surprise. Its simple, focused premise works perfectly for this type of film and allows for some solid technical execution. However, after a really strong setup it does begin to lose its way around halfway through. Still, Predators delivers enough bloody thrills to make it watchable for both fans of the franchise and of the action/horror genre.

727.title: Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery

metadata.tagline: When the game ends, the mystery begins.
metadata.original_title: Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery

727.rich_text:
Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery When the game ends, the mystery begins. Comedy Crime Mystery Rian Johnson Daniel Craig Edward Norton Janelle Monáe Kathryn Hahn Leslie Odom Jr. Kate Hudson Dave Bautista Jessica Henwick Madelyn Cline Noah Segan World-famous detective Benoit Blanc heads to Greece to peel back the layers of a mystery surrounding a tech billionaire and his eclectic crew of friends. Disappointing and convoluted, *Glass Onion* fails to match the charm and wit of the original. A muddled mystery with little impact. The worst mystery movie I've ever scene. When the twist comes the smartest detective in the world says "its so dumb, its sooo dumb", not even realizing he is the dumbest part of the whole movie. Without spoiling anything all I can say is after the twist he is either criminally reckless, or actually trying to kill the victim. While I can definitely see the problems that this movie has, it was a lot better than I remember it being and I still very much enjoyed it! Another decent film in this series, which is better than the first imho. Some of the jokes were better than the first film, and the acting was generally of a higher standard. I particularly like Monae, and this time Craig’s accent wasn’t as distracting. The direction and the narrative were ok, the plot however was easily guessed. I’d watch it again! The same puzzle, but more tedious.

'Glass Onion' is not better than its predecessor; it is weaker and less convincing, despite having a script that I consider denser. Johnson makes a misstep that the previous film avoided: a series of decisions based on coincidences that sometimes feel forced. It’s not poorly written, but it does stretch credibility.

It is less engaging and entertaining. The pace is noticeably slower, and this time the film relies more on the cast than on the story itself—a balance that was handled more effectively in the first film. While Craig brings his signature charisma and helps carry the ensemble (which is otherwise somewhat limited), Edward Norton does not stand out to me.

The set design, although eye-catching with a giant crystal onion, loses much of the impact seen in the previous installment. Still, Johnson avoids monotony with a narrative that feels distinct and “refreshing” within the same universe. The plot is slightly more intricate, and it’s clear that this is a scripted story, particularly in the way the characters formulate their theories.

It neither surpasses nor equals its predecessor; however, it does not disappoint. The film is solid, light, and enjoyable. Glass Onion isn't as good as the first one, but it's still an incredibly fun ride.

It has a very different setting, a very different set of characters and shows a different side of Benoit Blanc. Where the first felt classic, this one feels modern and I liked the first one more during the first and now too. Here the killer was more obvious and I always say that wasn't the point of this movie, but I still miss that kind of the big surprise, becauee there's still one in this film, which is awesome.

The directing is good, the tone of this is very different from the first one, but it works. The cinematography has even more playful camera movement, which I loved. The editing is "same-same, but different, but still same". The cast is still extremely strong, but in my opinion there's no outstanding performance besides Daniel Craig this time.

Glass Onion is the least amazing part of an incredible trilogy. Poorly acted in most places and cliched in all others.

Another case of Netflix paying for reviews on the internet. Universal acclaim with critics, a whole bunch of confused viewers who can't figure out why they're watching a B-movie mystery that's rated 81 by critics.

Done with online reviews. Chapter two of the Benoit Blanc mysteries, following in the footsteps of Knives Out with an (almost) entirely new cast that scarcely misses a beat. Just like its predecessor, Glass Onion is stuffed with brash characters, crafty double-crosses, silly scraps of intrigue and light-hearted japes at the expense of high society. Like a great magician, it delights in pulling the wool over the audience’s eyes, but doesn’t rely on cheap tricks or lies to conceal the truth. We’re merely convinced to avert our gaze each time the murder weapon stands exposed.

As with the original film, the first hour is a riotous joyride that’s often laugh-out-loud funny. The setup is ingenious and magical, a puzzle so deeply layered that, at first glance, it can be tough to discern when the real game has actually begun. It delights and surprises with wit and charm, wrenches the wheel every time we get comfortable, rewinds and revisits and rebuilds the facts to upend the truths we once held sacred. The home stretch gets a bit too crafty for my taste, continuing its erratic course when I was long-since ready to quit playing around, but that’s a problem I had with Knives Out, too, and I should’ve expected nothing less. It’s very much a case of more-of-the-same, and the lack of creative drop-off is impressive considering the plot’s complexities and the massive casting churn. Jamie Lee Curtis and Chris Evans might have gone missing, but Edward Norton, Kathryn Hahn and Dave Bautista are more than adequate replacements. And, now that I’ve grown accustomed to the accent, Daniel Craig’s southern sleuth serves as a superb master of ceremonies. Tons of fun. Cringe writing. Hard to focus on the plot given how ignorant the writers are about almost every topic discussed in the movie.

Overall a major regression from the first movie. While it fails to be a full-on murder mystery, that fact allows it to succeed as a unique film that explores modern wealth and its perceptions. On a first watch, the plot is snappy and unpredictable in the most enjoyable fashion, never engaging in a dull moment by using its reputation to keep viewers on their toes.

The cast all play their roles perfectly, each a believable stereotype that makes you love none of them but nonetheless invested in all of them. Danial Craig again delivers a masterclass of a performance as Benoit Blanc in this satirical and comedic film.

When they decide to play, they are immediately sucked into the jungle world of Jumanji in the bodies of their avatars. They’ll have to complete the adventure of their lives filled with fun, thrills and danger or be stuck in the game forever! Cool actors, cool antagonist and cool effects. It's a good movie about students and idk, what else can I say. Pleasant film with a simple but well developed and entertaining story. The only critic I can find about this movie is its streamlined nature. But it's not like Stranger Things. Storywriting isn't perfect but it's better than I expected for a movie of this kind. A big budget, mainstream action/comedy from Hollywood that follows all the usual tropes. Entertaining enough but not that memorable. A really good film, you should watch it if you can. (I have seen the first movie and I liked it, but this is better) This movie totally missed the point of the original Jumanji and tried to do something more ''modern'' and ''new'' but unfortunately the humor was stale the animations and effects were average and the story was just an boring trip  with no epic scenes. Remember the last dice throw from the original movie man that was just amazing and everything about the scene was epic but here there was no such thing.Average movie that is an insult to the original should've just named the movie something else. I love this movie and actors!

729.title: The Croods: A New Age

metadata.tagline: The future ain't what it used to be.

729.rich_text:
The Croods: A New Age The Croods: A New Age The future ain't what it used to be. Animation Family Adventure Fantasy Comedy Joel Crawford Nicolas Cage Emma Stone Ryan Reynolds Catherine Keener Cloris Leachman Clark Duke Leslie Mann Peter Dinklage Kelly Marie Tran Kailey Crawford Searching for a safer habitat, the prehistoric Crood family discovers an idyllic, walled-in paradise that meets all of its needs. Unfortunately, they must also learn to live with the Bettermans -- a family that's a couple of steps above the Croods on the evolutionary ladder. As tensions between the new neighbors start to rise, a new threat soon propels both clans on an epic adventure that forces them to embrace their differences, draw strength from one another, and survive together. Another agreeable outing for the titular prehistoric clan, The Croods: A New Age may be the missing link for parents between more elevated family-friendly fare. To kill **** story with a good premise so badly just for the sake of money is unbelievably awful. Not only did the interesting characters become just formulaic, but also the main plot of the crisis of the film (about bananas) makes no sense as it was already overcome in the first part. The attempt to make something teenage out of a children's cautionary tale became a complete failure. The change of director and screenwriters was a huge mistake. To be honest, I could only watch the cartoon in its entirety on the third try. I don't recommend it. Did not expect to enjoy this as much as I did. Was anyone really begging for a sequel to The Croods? I know they got a Netflix series but every DreamWorks movie gets a **** Netflix series these days. Were toy sales that high? Did their new Universal overlords demand it?

Whatever the reason, The Croods: A New Age is better than its **** practically every way. The animation is rich with vibrant colours and lively cinematography, several of the characters go through well-defined arcs, it's very funny, it's heartwarming, the new cast members are delightful, and I didn't always know where the plot was going. I am genuinely surprised. It feels weird that I'm saying this but Grug has quickly become one of my favourite DreamWorks characters; I just find the guy really endearing and Nicolas Cage is perfect in the role.

It's still not among the studio's very best, but I think many people will really grow to appreciate this sequel as an underrated gem as the years pass. And you don't even have to see the first movie to fully enjoy this one! But honestly you might as well, because that's valuable Grug time that you would be missing out on. Any Grug time is time well spent. This was amazing, when I finished to watch it, the only thing that I wanted to do was watching it again. When we watched the movie on the cinema we laugh out loud from the hilarious humor that it has. One of the best comedy films I've ever seen. Okay, we (partner and our entire extended adult family) *love* The (original) Croods. Somehow never heard about it until we caught it on Netflix last spring. And then it was so wholesome, hilarious, entertaining and GORGEOUS from start to finish! I mean, we were just looking for a somewhat entertaining way to chill through a hangover when we found it, but what we got was such a treat! It immediately became one of our absolute favorites.

Turn to Croods 2: WHAAAT?!

It's perfect!!!

Couldn't believe how much we loved this entire movie - obviously it was as good as the original, but maybe even *better*??

Seriously, the whole thing was so creative and entertaining and the addition of new cast was a perfect fit!

The *best* thing about this movie (and I don't think it's a spoiler - it's in the trailers) is that they turned the played out and awful jealous-girls-fighting-over-a-(literal)-Guy thing completely on its head. And they set it up so well! "Oh no, Dawn and Guy have history? Oh no, they're even saying the same things at the same time? Aaah, and their matching lemur accessories just thrust them together?? Oh nooo!"

And then. Annnnd then. What immediately blossoms between Eep and Dawn was such a *welcome* surprise, not to mention heartwarming and realistic ("Why are our voices getting so high-pitched - Eeeeee!" Hahaha, teen memories).

It was so *refreshing* to see that kind of healthy female friendship relationship portrayed and developed, especially with a "Guy" involved.

Meanwhile, the whole Croods family just being themselves is great. Grug's biggest problem (as ever) is that he just loves too dang much. That's incredibly endearing for a literal "cave-man" character.

And by the end of the movie? Oh, it is all wrapped up so nicely I wanna put a bow on it. It's so happy! The creators described wanting to make this movie a "celebration" of the Croods characters. And they achieved that splendidly. It's hard to think of any other stories so full of *joy.*

So yeah, I'm leaving out a lot because I don't want to include any spoilers, but this is one of those rare cases where in making a sequel - they absolutely NAILED it.

This movie is a gem. I don't think I've seen anything else that makes you feel so completely happy at the end. And for that, if *anybody* who was involved in this movie's creation ever happens to see this, I just want to say THANK YOU for this gift of a movie!! (*Especially* right now.) Thank you.

I'm gonna go watch it again. I had a ton of fun watching this movie. Laughed out loud several times.
Just a good fun entertainment. +Great 4k hdr presentation
+Superb voice cast
+Great pacing
+Entertaining screenplay
-Story was pretty weak

All things considered croods new age is a decent sequel and entertaining way to pass the time. It was an ok movie, had a bit of comedy but otherwise kind of boring. The story didn't really make sense, the plot was random and it got corny a lot of times. I only liked the funny parts, and my family likes it too. My dad didn't enjoy it though.

I'm giving this a 5. 7/12

It was cute and some of the childish jokes got me more than they should’ve. Also, I haven’t seen the first one so I’m missing out on any of that context. But, this was easy enough to understand on its own. Kids will love it and adults can enjoy it enough to sit through.

730.title: Source Code

metadata.tagline: Make every second count.

730.rich_text:
Source Code Source Code Make every second count. Thriller Science Fiction Mystery Duncan Jones Jake Gyllenhaal Michelle Monaghan Vera Farmiga Jeffrey Wright Michael Arden Cas Anvar Russell Peters Brent Skagford Craig Thomas Gordon Masten When decorated soldier Captain Colter Stevens wakes up in the body of an unknown man, he discovers he's part of a mission to find the bomber of a Chicago commuter train. A relentless race through fragmented time: A 4.0-star thriller that mastered the rhythm of repetition.110504 (4.0)I watched this in the theater in 2011. The concept of revisiting the last eight minutes of someone else's life to stop a disaster was incredibly gripping. Unlike other "time loop" movies that can feel repetitive, this one kept increasing the stakes with every jump. It had that "chewy" tension and sharp, rhythmic pacing I love—where every second felt calculated and vital. A solid 4.0 for a smart, high-energy sci-fi thriller that didn't waste a single moment of its runtime. Like INCEPTION, this is one of the few movies that you can't spoil since even the smallest detail could accidentally reveal a twist or two. The story itself is a very original blend of thriller, sci-fi and drama and it works. Full of unseen twists and with a high octane pacing, SOURCE CODE will keep you wanting for more as each answer is slowly revealed. The script helps too but its the actors, who deliver the lines well, who drive the movie into emotional levels. My only problem with the film is some weak foreshadowing but it thankfully doesn't affect the movie in a bad way and to give any more details would spoil the **** keep it short and to avoid accidentally spoiling a plot detail or two, SOURCE CODE is a must watch. It's one of the few original films out there in a market full of crap and it's definitely worth your money. It's just a pity that Hollywood doesn't seem to be supporting these kinds of films. Yeah, it didn't interest me for one second. I had high hopes because Moon by the same director was rather excellent, but this is such a mess of old terrain that is not improved by the director's approach. From an official film critic who reviewed this movie, a particularly funny and memorable line: "Gyllenhaal is particularly unsuited to this role, his saucer eyes flashing from calm to crazed. In the not-at-all-distant future, the US military runs a trial of their new time travel tech. By way of a loosely-explained new breakthrough, they're able to inject an unwitting agent into the near past, where he relives the eight minutes immediately preceding a terrorist attack over and over again, desperately seeking suspects and answers.

I'm typically a big fan of this style of high-concept science fiction, and for the great majority of its running time, Source Code manages to continuously one-up itself in that respect. The film doesn't shy away from delivering powerful, surprising answers as events repeatedly play themselves out, while a deep, complex script ensures there's always a new mystery to pick up where the last one left off. With a nice juicy carrot dangling just out of reach and a breakneck pace from start to finish, this feels more like an intense, brilliant short film and not the feature-length offering it actually is. Though an awkward, mismatched happy ending does sour things to a certain extent, the sharp curves it navigates before running into that wall won't be easily forgotten. Well overall I actually enjoyed my experience but it’s not consistent enjoyment. I very much enjoyed Source Code, though I feel like the film loses a bit of steam near the end. Kosala Andreas Katsulas Wrongfully convicted of murdering his wife and sentenced to death, Richard Kimble escapes from the law in an attempt to find the real killer and clear his name. The Fugitive is by far Harrison Ford and Tommy Lee Jones best films. The whole movie is captivating and every time it is on TV, or if I ever see the film on an airplanes film selection, I know 2 hours will fly by. The Fugitive is an incredibly well paced action thriller featuring two great actors at the top of their game. Great thriller with fantastic acting and pacing. A true classic! One of Harrison Ford and Tommy Lee Jones' best films. This is a movie everyone should see at least once. Even without knowing the series that inspired it, the film has enough to hold the viewer's attention, which is more than welcome. To watch with a big bag of popcorn. Ford and Jones do a great job in this one. I didn't like the cliche of the bad guys not killing their target when they have the chance, but other than that, this is a good movie. The acting and pacing were solid throughout. A good measured film, does not let you get bored and makes you feel worried about the main character.
The only thing that is very weakly shown in my opinion is the bitterness over the loss. Harrison Ford and Tommy Lee Jones race around in circles for this memorable early '90s cat-and-mouse blockbuster, skillfully adapting and modernizing a four-season television series from thirty years prior. The Fugitive doesn't fool around, racing through dozens of heavy plot points in the first hour without feeling overwhelming or hyperactive. It's a succinct, condensed version of a once-sprawling serial, one which trims away the obligatory TV padding without skipping any good bits.

While it's trucking through those establishing shots, the story is a whiplash stunner; in the blink of an eye, we see our protagonist as a respected physician, grieving husband, bewildered murder suspect, sentenced convict, opportunistic escapee and outdoor survivalist, with one particularly well-executed train derailment thrown in to really kick off all the turmoil. Almost by necessity, the second act slows down to focus on the chase, balancing Ford's attempts to lay low with Jones's top-of-the-food-chain detective work. That performs well, too, a firm gear-shift from the opening salvo’s manic mayhem (one that's certainly assisted by its two phenomenal cornerstone stars), though it does lose its way as all the different points converge and the moment of resolution draws near. By contrast, the ending falls more on the bland, derivative side; careful suspense cast aside in favor of a big chair-tossing, pipe-swinging, rock'em'sock'em finale. These scenes are inoffensive, but a decided step down from what we'd seen and felt just prior. Put it this way: I still vividly recalled the bus crash and dam jump, decades after I last saw them. I'd forgotten all about the climactic rooftop fist fight.

While the gettin's good, it's real good. A fairly simple premise with plenty of intrigue and gray morality, a tight script, more than one all-decade action set, a super-sized portion of Tommy Lee Jones intensity and lots and lots of chances for grim Harrison Ford to glance worriedly over his shoulder. Maybe not perfect, but it still holds up. Чудовий фільм. Подібного багато, але я прихильник актора Форда, тому я подивився з великим задоволенням. Всім рекомендую. Ghost Ghost Before Sam was murdered, he told Molly he'd love and protect her forever. Fantasy Thriller Romance Jerry Zucker Patrick Swayze Demi Moore Whoopi Goldberg Tony Goldwyn Vincent Schiavelli Rick Aviles Martina Deignan Rick Kleber Phil Leeds Armelia McQueen After a young man is murdered, his spirit stays behind to warn his lover of impending danger, with the help of a reluctant psychic. The most beautiful love story in cinema?

Without exaggeration, this is one of the most beautiful films I have ever seen. Not only because of what is told, but because of how it is told. There is a very clear narrative and emotional precision throughout. Produced, written, and directed with a level of accuracy and excellence that is almost intimidating. Jerry Zucker demonstrates supreme control over tone and rhythm. He knows exactly what he wants to say and how he wants me to feel as a viewer. He knows when to cut and when to let a scene breathe, all with a sense of vertiginous natural flow. The scenes that move toward sex stop at exactly the right point, reminding you that this is a film about love, not about making love.

The transitions deserve a specific mention. They are genuine narrative magic tricks: when I think one thing is happening, it suddenly becomes something entirely different, flipping the whole scene on its head and leaving me with my hands over my face.

Patrick Swayze and Demi Moore deliver exquisite, deeply human performances. No excess, no overacting. Everything flows naturally. Their chemistry is undeniable—a connection that feels authentic and reaches beyond the screen. A truly endearing relationship.

The visual effects are noticeable and clearly dated, but they are better integrated than I expected. They aim to serve the story rather than overwhelm it with spectacle. The music becomes the film’s true leitmotif. Every time I hear 'Unchained Melody', I will think of this film. Exquisite music, emotionally intelligent, accompanying the scenes without ever overpowering them.

What truly makes this film special is its message: emotional permanence, grief, acceptance of reality, and the idea that love does not strictly end with death. A direct challenge to the notion of “till death do us part.” Love is presented as an omnipresent force that goes beyond limits and certainties. Love remains, even when the person is no longer there. A reflection on learning to let go, on how a genuine bond does not disappear, but transforms.

A Warm, Resilient Portrait of a Life Shaped by Family and the Magic of Cinema251010 (4.7)The temperature **** that loves film, family, and the beauty of life is felt throughout this masterpiece. I was deeply moved by the comfort of a story that feels thoroughly warmed and firmly baked by experience. The title "The Fabelmans," carrying the double meaning of a storyteller, is a brilliant choice—especially as it functions as a typical Jewish surname while masking the director's autobiography. The film portrays a harmonious and wealthy household with such warmth that it is impossible to feel anything but a pleasant envy. Seeing the siblings film together in their youth and continue to support each other’s cinematic journeys in adulthood is heartwarming. The director's meticulousness in seeking his siblings' approval and waiting until his parents' passing to release the film out of respect for their feelings shows a profound sensitivity. While the upbringing—born to an artist mother and an engineer father, moving westward toward the promised land of cinema—seems ideal, the film doesn't shy away from the pain of his mother's bold affair. It is interesting to ponder why the young protagonist initially resented his father for the divorce, considering his mother remarried her lover the following year, but the film captures the complexity of these emotions beautifully. The stoic realization that "the show must go on" even when the family is torn apart, as Uncle Boris suggested, highlights the relentless nature of the artistic calling. This artistic drive is even shown when the protagonist captures his bully on film because he looks good in the frame—a moment where art transcends personal spite. The appearance of David Lynch as the legendary John Ford was a delightful surprise; watching him enjoy a cigar was bittersweet, given Lynch's recent health struggles. The ending, where the horizon is realigned to signify that the upcoming journey will be even more exciting, was absolutely charming. This film is a kind and generous love letter to cinema that doesn't feel childish or exclusionary to non-cinephiles. It feels like a masterfully prepared meal that goes down smoothly without unnecessary seasoning, leaving the heart feeling comforted and warm with a smile that never leaves the face. Rewatching Black Hawk Down after so many years is more striking than I expected. Not because the violence shocks more now, but because of how relentless it still feels. The film never slows down, never explains itself, and never gives you room to breathe. From the very first moment, it throws you into the middle of the chaos and refuses to let go until the end.Ridley Scott abandons the classic structure of war movies. There are no clean emotional arcs, no heroic speeches, and very little personal backstory. Instead, everything is confusion, noise, dust, and split-second decisions. Some might find it cold or distant, but that approach turns the viewing experience into something almost physical. You’re not observing the battle — you’re stuck inside ****’s not an anti-war statement in the traditional sense, nor is it a straightforward glorification. It simply shows what happens. That uncomfortable neutrality is precisely what makes it so effective and so divisive. The film doesn’t guide your emotions; it leaves you alone in the **** ensemble cast works as a single unit rather than individual stars, reinforcing the sense of anonymity and exhaustion. Faces blend together, priorities blur, and survival becomes the only narrative thread. Technically, the film remains overwhelming — from the sound design to the editing — creating constant tension that rarely ****’s not an easy rewatch, and it’s not meant to be. But even decades later, its intensity and commitment to immersion remain undeniable. Black Hawk Down is one of the best war movies i have ever seen. Ex Machina Ex Machina There is nothing more human than the will to survive. Drama Science Fiction Alex Garland Domhnall Gleeson Alicia Vikander Oscar Isaac Sonoya Mizuno Corey Johnson Claire Selby Symara A. Templeman Gana Bayarsaikhan Tiffany Pisani Elina Alminas Caleb, a coder at the world's largest internet company, wins a competition to spend a week at a private mountain retreat belonging to Nathan, the reclusive CEO of the company. But when Caleb arrives at the remote location he finds that he will have to participate in a strange and fascinating experiment in which he must interact with the world's first true artificial intelligence, housed in the body of a beautiful robot girl. "Ex Machina" is visually impeccable, isolated and intelligent science fiction film that quietly thrills its audience and leaves them thinking. First time director Alex Garland who has written numerous sci-fi stories has surprising skill, with direction that simply feels masterful. His sense of pace, space, and control over all elements of film is rare. It's not even that one has to read deeply into the film to find how great Garland is, the skill is just felt and that's what watching great filmmakers feels like.

The atmosphere of the film stands out tremendously, with art direction that has a futuristic style, and cinematography to enhance it. There are reflections everywhere, and Oscar Isaac's house, despite its cleanness, feels claustrophobic in a maze-like way. Even just blank walls have so much character to them. These reflections give us the sense that we don't truly know the intents of the characters. The film twists like a thriller as it unfolds. It's confined and explosive.

We are stuck on Isaac's estate with just three characters who form a complex and ambiguous character triangle. Domhnall Gleeson is mostly good in his role, but sometimes has unrealistic moments of awkwardness. Oscar Isaac is fantastic and very funny in a way we can probably relate to others we've met. He's the kind of guy who tries to make you feel more comfortable than you want to feel. His character's genius also comes off, and so does his bluntness. All of these characteristics wrap up in a full and understandable, if detached, human being. Also great is rising star Alicia Vikander as Ava, who is believable as an A.I, and that's saying a lot. Her movements are very subtly off-kilter, and her soul is ambiguous.

The film has ideas on its mind as well about the possibility of artificial intelligence and what weaknesses humans have when put up against them. For me, some of the A.I. ideas felt too familiar, and by the end I felt like the movie was saying something I'd kind of heard before. On the other hand, the flaw of humanity that the film reveals was very effective and new. The metaphor with the Jackson Pollock painting sticks in my mind. This is one of the more exciting sci-fi films in recent memory. It's physically small, but as intense as any big budget flick and with many more ideas and masterful visuals. 2010 ve sonrasının "Yapay zekanın insana karşı olması" temalı yapımlarının ilki ya da en popüleri olan yapım. Comedy Dave Chernin, John Chernin Mason Thames Ramon Reed Raphael Alejandro Isabella Ferreira Bardia Seiri Loren Gray Ali Gallo Scott MacArthur Thomas Barbusca Kim Hawthorne Their first week of high school. The biggest party of the year. Mistakes will be made as four teenage boys navigate a night of mayhem and debauchery. It's like if Superbad, was super bad.

'Incoming' is the latest of Netflix's attempts to appeal to a younger audience - this time with a movie that follows the same general plot points we've seen in every single party movie since Seth Rogan's 2007 classic. 
Guy meets a girl, starts acting like a crazed maniac to try and get her to like him, she falls out of love, and he wins her back by demonstrating what a silly goofy wacky wild character he is and that he should have never tried to change who he is - blah blah blah we've seen it a million times.
This lack of creativity combined with the movie's often crude, slapstick and at certain times even downright disgusting humour make for a watching experience akin to that of 2018's 'The Package'.
In summary, this movie perfectly demonstrates that the corporate-supervised writing typically seen in Netflix movies does not mix well with the concept of a party movie, relying on shock value to bring any excitement and distract from the film's stale overused plot points and uninteresting stereotypical characters. Pretty funny movie. It's not Shakespeare, but nobody wanted it to be.. It's exactly right for a funny evening. For as long as I can remember, there have been a handful of coming-of-age adolescent comedies. Some are memorable, others not so much; however, you would be hard-pressed to find a more popular raunchy comedy than 2007's Superbad. It's a film so ingrained in pop culture. It overtook classics like 1982's Fast Times at Ridgemont High or 1984's Revenge of the Nerds. Before Superbad, the millennial generation grew up with 1999's American Pie. With "Incoming," Directors/Writers Dave Chernin and John Chernin aim to bring you the Gen Z update of coming-of-age movies. While the argument certainly can be made that "Incoming" is reminiscent of "Superbad," I would hardly call it a knockoff or updated version of that film. There are similarities, but both films have different approaches to handling the core cast (Mason Thames, Ramon Reed, Raphael Alejandro, and Bardia Seiri). They have different goals and wants than the boys in "Superbad." Although not entirely original, I found it fun and often laughed at the numerous jokes throughout the film. The cast of 'Incoming' is exceptional, with each member bringing their unique energy to the film. Their chemistry is palpable, and Bobby Cannavale's performance is particularly noteworthy. I highly recommend 'Incoming' to anyone looking for a fun time and a few solid laughs. Set during the dawn of the modern United States (in Pennsylvania), his wife joins him, and their lives are forever changed by a demanding, wealthy patron. The lesson of this movie, movingly communicated, seems to be that brutalism is more than an architectural style; it can also be a lifestyle, one that persists into the present era. Perhaps it is fundamental to human nature that some individuals consider the end goal more important than how one gets there. I would love to make a lasting contribution to humanity's collection of precious objects, but not if the path is littered with drugs, alcohol, broken relationships, ruined dreams, and a total unwillingness to compromise. Sadly, many of those at the helm seem to be brutalists by nature. The rest of us can only gape at the slaughter, or, perhaps, lie down in front of the bulldozers. ¿Por dónde comenzar?, película que debe reunir ciertos elementos y un check list para ser políticamente correcta y cumplir los estándares poco variados de los oscar... tal vez??; ya se: hagamos una interpretación de un pobrecito inmigrante (judio para variar por supuesto), que llega a la Nueva York de los finales de los años 40, además en la postguerra; además agreguemos un tinte de poeta maldito para sea más seguro el oscar. Eso en resumen es esta cinta. No aporta nada nuevo. Dura más de 3 horas sin que se sienta ningún progreso ni en los personajes y casi que ni en la misma película. Como siempre: ricos muy malos y pobres muy buenos. Y esta lejisimos de ser trasgresor y antisistema, creo que más bien es un súbdito a las ideas del capitalismo en sus planteamientos. Lo más grave es la falta completa de relación con el nombre del Brutalista; donde quedó la arquitectura, donde quedó la academia y las decenas de obras resaltantes de esta corriente. This non-linear storytelling enhances the emotional impact, reinforcing how the weight of history shapes the course of one’s artistic journey. The sound design and score play a crucial role in shaping the film’s emotional rhythm. Retro musical choices provide moments of nostalgia and relief, easing viewers into the narrative while preparing them for the more emotionally resonant sequences that follow. A key technical highlight in The Brutalist is the integration of VistaVision, this format plays a crucial role in enhancing the film’s visual language, particularly in its depiction of architecture and character-driven moments. The Brutalist is a meditative, visually captivating film that draws you into its world with a quiet, immersive intensity. Its deliberate storytelling and hypnotic cinematography create a deeply emotional experience, while raw, controlled performances anchor its meditative pace. The minimalist setting and evocative score perfectly complement the film’s themes of isolation and introspection. Despite its long runtime, the film never loses its grip, leaving a lingering, thoughtful impact.

I may not be religious, but I believe this is the golden standard for religious movies. The art and portrayal of the characters is captivating throughout the film. The animation gives weight to the powers of God used in the story which is only enhanced by the incredible music displayed. Most of the scenes could be screenshotted and hung as a work of art on its own. Although some minor scenes may be hard to understand without prior context, this film does a great job at keeping the main plot digestible. A downright incredible experience throughout. The phenomenal art direction and animation quality push this film to iconic levels. The superb cast and soundtrack work extremely well in breathing life into its characters. Something feels a little off with the pacing and the musical segments fell a bit flat for me. Overall this was a very enjoyable watch. Is the bible outdated? The truth is that yes, that is why it is surprising that Dreamworks made one of its best productions based on one of the best-known passages from this book, a movie that you should see at least once in your life, even more so if you are a fan of animation. An amazing movie!! Great music, I mean Whitney Houston and Mariah Carey, amazing. I love the original story so the movie is even better. I adore this movie. It is a great masterpiece from Dreamworks and an animated gem, the animation is amazing, the cinematography and story are great and the music is very memorable and what makes the movie itself stand out the most, it is absolutely excellent and an animated masterpiece that combines the story and religion and this is a great example of non-Disney animated movies. However, it almost became a milestone in cinema (although it was not), but it did become another milestone in the history of the animation genre, although the previous animated films without being from Disney in the early 80s and 90s tried to be animated films from different non-Disney studios and receiving in some animated films in box office failures and critics in some occasions (with the passage of time, they would be able to be appreciated to some non-Disney animated films), but The Prince of Egypt changed everything by giving us the most memorable songs, the emotional soundtrack, the most exciting story, the superior animation and cinematography and as a result the critics love it so much and the box office managed to be an absolute success with 218 million. dollars worldwide becoming one of the highest grossing films of the year 1998 and thanks to that The Prince of Egypt managed to be the great success in the history of animated cinema in general l both critically and at the box office and is currently considered an animated classic and one of the best non-Disney animated movies. This movie is a great animated gem that is always a magnificent experience for animated movies, an animated gem that will never be **** Prince of Egypt is the film that managed to be the first great milestone in the cinema of non-Disney animated films, and it is the Dreamworks animated film that manages to highlight the story and is Dreamworks' "The Lion King". This is by far the greatest animated movie of all time in my opinion. The animation is amazing, the voice actors are brilliant, the music is excellent, the characters are likeable, I just love everything about this movie. I just wished dreamworks did more movies like this. I know we have The Road to El Dorado but that was pretty mediocre. Also there is Joseph King of Dreams but I haven't watched that yet but it actually looks good. Anyways this is the greatest animated movie ever. I definitely recommend this movie to anyone. No me pareció una película espectacular como muchos dicen, pero definitivamente entiendo porque algunos la consideran un clásico. A nivel de animación cumple muy bien, no es la mejor, pero definitivamente llega a ser muy atractivo incluso a día de hoy. A nivel de historia, esta película se beneficiaria mas si sabes sobre la historia real de la biblia, aunque la película hace todo lo posible para que entiendas en caso de que seas como yo que no leyó nada de nada, y sigue funcionando muy bien como historia en si, sin embargo si es cierto que varios elementos de la historia original según tengo entendido no están presentes, pero no lo tomare en cuenta como un punto negativo ya que igual la película esta bien contada dentro de su sencillez. Hay algunos pequeños huecos argumentales, pero nada grave, en resumen, esta bastante bien. No es la mejor de Dreamworks, pero los personajes e historia son realmente memorables y ha envejecido bastante bien, y eso es lo único que importa. I love DreamWorks and for some reason The Prince of Egypt passed me by. So I had to fix it and I can't complain. Right from the first moment the animation appealed to me, which in my opinion had its own charm and I found it just beautiful. Add to that the sometimes epic music by Hans Zimmer and a great story. For me, a great film that I recommend, especially to Egypt lovers, because I personally really like Egypt and for me this film was a wonderful spectacle.

757.title: Terrifier 3

metadata.tagline: Prepare to be terrified again.

757.rich_text:
Terrifier 3 Terrifier 3 Prepare to be terrified again. Horror Thriller Damien Leone Lauren LaVera David Howard Thornton Samantha Scaffidi Elliott Fullam Margaret Anne Florence Bryce Johnson Alexa Blair Robertson Antonella Rose Mason Mecartea Krsy Fox Five years after surviving Art the Clown's Halloween massacre, Sienna and Jonathan are still struggling to rebuild their shattered lives. As the holiday season approaches, they try to embrace the Christmas spirit and leave the horrors of the past behind. But just when they think they're safe, Art returns, determined to turn their holiday cheer into a new nightmare. The festive season quickly unravels as Art unleashes his twisted brand of terror, proving that no holiday is safe. The story here is stupid, our 'protagonist' is included in none of the plot or action until at least the 95 minute mark.Hate these movies at this point. And this is somehow the modern day franchise of my favorite genre. I had a bad but funny experience when I saw Terrifier. Last November I went to the movies with a guy named Agustín, he asked me if I wanted to see that movie and I said yes even though I hadn't seen the previous two; he had told me there were violent scenes but I didn't think much of **** had some problems before entering the theater because we lost our tickets, but then we found them, bought popcorn and some **** sat in the middle because I couldn't see very well; the boys next to us were talking very loudly while using their cell phones.When the movie had already started, almost everyone fell silent except for the girls who were behind **** film told the story of Sienna and her brother who survived the last massacre of Art the clown who is a demon. It didn't make much sense since the whole movie was based on close-up brutal murders and torture.That was one of the reasons why I didn't like the movie; the acting was quite bad and we laughed a lot about it. The seats were very comfortable, but the sound was very loud.Despite that, we had a lot of fun, we laughed, ate, drank and had a good time. When the movie ended, there was a man dressed as Art at the door and he scared us a lot.Afterwards we ate hamburgers and had ice cream at McDonald's, I called my dad and he came to pick me up at 10pm. New holiday classic just dropped and it contains the best use of chainsaws since TCM 2 and the best use of liquid nitrogen since Jason X. The moviegoing experience wasn't exactly what I idealized in my head but I should have expected a mostly empty theater at 10 PM on a Monday. The few people there didn't seem to enjoy it nearly as much as I did since I overheard a couple complaining about how nothing made sense and that this is basically how "generic horror films are". Well, I might be missing something if this really is the norm for horror films coming out because I don't believe I've ever watched anything as gory and violent in theaters ever. 

Let's be honest, the plot and mythology are merely incidental in the Terrifier franchise. I like Sienna a lot and her relationship with her family is fun and endearing, but the reason I'm here is to se Art do his thing so I can smile like a madman and laugh at the cartoony brutality of it all. It's pretty appropriate that the last film I watched before T3 was The Party because this is basically structured like a silly 60's comedy: a bunch of vignettes connected by a thin plot that exists to justify its gags. The difference is that the the audience does the whole gagging part because boy oh boy the deaths in this are wild. It's so over the top with loose body parts and blood, I love it so much. It's disgusting, the one with the rats made me feel sick for a few seconds. I can't stop thinking about that Jennifer introduction in Pig Destroyer's Prowler in the Yard. 

"This is disgusting, it's pornography."

"No, no, no. This is beautiful, this is art."

This is pretty much my thing, at times it felt like one of those gory and sleazy Italian Horror flicks from the 80's, or at least what you think some of them might be like when you look at the cover art. The ending sequence with that red glowing hole to hell or whatever plus the glowing possessed demon eyes and Holy Mary holding a chained rando evil dude with a mask forging the powerful sword feels like the kind of Italian insanity to me, idk. That cold opening is great, pretty Black Christmas-y or that one Santa episode from the Tales From the Crypt TV show (I think it's called And All Through the House), but much more sadistic. Art has no boundaries regarding who he inflicts pain on. I can't even choose which kill is my favorite, they are all so creative and unique and gory and gross and beautiful. 

I can't stress enough how much I loved this, every kill a work of Art, brutal and hilarious, cartoon violence if it had blood and guts. Had the time of my life watching it and no one can take this away from me. 

Now please take Art to space in the next movie. This movie wasn't exactly the worst, but father god, it was confusing. The story felt all over the place and didn't feel consistent with the previous films. The characters also did feel fairly fleshed out but not enough to get attached to them or even like them besides Sienna, but she's the protagonist, so that's kind ****. I think the thing I liked the least about this movie wasn't the lackluster story or bland characters, but the over-the-top and un-neccessarily overdone gore. Like I've never genuinely been on the verge of throwing up before watching this and I mean that in any way but a good way. Terrifier 3 was an excellent film. I especially appreciated the gore, as the killing scenes were so intense they made you want to look away. The antagonist is truly a disturbing and twisted character. Unlike many horror movies that fail to deliver genuine scares, Terrifier succeeds in creating an atmosphere of real horror. The signature creepy grin and unsettling wave from the Terrifier consistently send chills down your spine.I thoroughly enjoyed this installment in the series. However, a warning: the movie does contain scenes of self-harm, which may be triggering for some viewers. With that in mind, I would still highly recommend this film to fans of the genre. 5 second TikTok IQ brainrot x gore. Society is falling when a film like this gets above a 5. It's a movie for 2 generations of idiots who enjoy Minecraft and **** and can't do 2 minutes of cardio or 5 straight pushups. Absolute ****. Completly bad. Don't watch or press the button x2 its better. You can also do something else onthe side and don't watch it, at least you will miss nothing. Terrifier 3 è un buon prodotto.
Il 2o migliore della trilogia dopo il primo, si può considerare un'opera riuscita dall'abile Damien Leone.
Le scene gore sono abbondanti, ben fatte e super violente, la regia è discreta, la performance degli attori è buona e il villain di Art si riconferma molto carismatico.
Il film è scorrevole e quando si arriva ai titoli di coda sembra di avere iniziato il film qualche minuto prima.
Consigliato If gore, some horror, and a below-average plot are enough to entertain you for about an hour and a half, then go for it. Terrifier 3 does not add much, but it does continue a story, all while keeping the doors open for more. TR3, however, does bring back what its audience may only be asking for: absurdly over-the-top kill sequences. Ещё больше изощрённых убийств и пыток, ещё больше крови и всего сопутствующего. Всё это происходит в замечательный и семейный рождественский праздник, ляпота. Сюжетная линия есть и тайна происхождения Арта почти раскрыта. Актёрская игра хороша, саунды шикарны. Отличный выбор для семейного просмотраЖду, с нетерпением 4-ую часть

758.title: Us

metadata.tagline: Watch yourself.

758.rich_text:
Us Us Watch yourself. Horror Mystery Jordan Peele Lupita Nyong'o Winston Duke Elisabeth Moss Tim Heidecker Shahadi Wright Joseph Evan Alex Yahya Abdul-Mateen II Anna Diop Cali Sheldon Noelle Sheldon Husband and wife Gabe and Adelaide Wilson take their kids to their beach house expecting to unplug and unwind with friends. But as night descends, their serenity turns to tension and chaos when some shocking visitors arrive uninvited. This film is absolutely atrocious; the plot, acting, and situations are laughable. It tries to be serious, terrifying, but it's actually quite absurd. I don't understand how anyone in their right mind could have enjoyed this disgrace. The more Jordan Peele’s films progress, the less logical they become.There are clearly ideas, but they’re never well executed. The social allegory isn’t interesting at all — when you find out who the Tethered are, you just sigh with boredom.There are way too many things that make no sense, simply because Peele didn’t know how to explain them and figured nobody would **** the final twist? It just made me shrug — nothing new. "Us" is a good horror film, albeit not a brilliant one. It lacks the convincing hopelessness that the doom evoked by the "Reds" evokes. Although the acting, particularly that of Lupida Nyong'o, is convincing, the film is predictable and drifts somewhat into a bloodthirsty zombie spectacle. Therefore, it doesn't quite do justice to the well-intentioned story of presenting people with their own self as a mirror image. Furthermore, the resolution of the storyline at the end somewhat lacks logic. This is my first Peele's work that I watch and I want to say that there are a lot of plot twist, thrilling and a lot of hidden messages that inspires the film like the bible verse or the hands across America. Us is a movie that is not ment to be interpreted literally, but the plot doesn't really make sense when you interpret it literally.

The characters are great, the family feels like a real one, with a funny, but a little careless dad; an overprotective mom and unique kids. The story is intriguing and it has an amazing twist, that I couldn't predict until the moments before it was revealed, but when I thought into the motivations of the characters, the plot just didn't make sense. That's why I watched a few explaining videos and found out that the plot is not meant to be the focus, but the themes. I understand that, but it's not to my liking.

The cinematography and direction are great, I love how Jordan Peele movies are shot. The acting performances are good too, but these things doesn't save the movie from being okay, at least for me.

Us looks great, it has a great plot twist, but the story doesn't make sense. I liked this movie for the wrong reasons. This was hilarious but it was supposed to be serious. As a horror, it wasn't scary, and was mostly just mindless gore and killing. Most of the movie was pretty funny, and the twist at the end was kind of interesting. But, other than that, nothing else was really that good. So, 6/10 This is the stupidest movie i have ever seen. The characters act foolishly and the villains are non consistent in their behaviour. Most of the times the characters get to live because they got lucky.
I know there should be a social commentary, but jesus can we have a watchable movie in the meantime pls?
Im so bored so i decided to write this instead of paying full attention to the movie. Im 90 minutes in amd honestly this movie should have ended 30 minutes ago. I somehow managed to miss this on release and before today had never had the opportunity to see it. Glad I caught it. The sort of film M Night Shyalaman wishes he was making. Throughly enjoyable. Peele understandably used his goodwill from Get Out to go for broke with a high-concept outing.  It doesn't always land.  The story folds under its own weight and is outright indecipherable at times.  Goodness, the man can direct a motion picture, though.  Gorgeous shots, great performances.  There's a thematic richness that ultimately shines brighter than the messy plot.  Worth seeing because the good bits are really, really good. Us. Me and my Shadow. A horror film from director Jordan Peele that evokes fear and provokes deep thought. The film skillfully combines elements of thriller, mystery and social commentary, creating a mysterious and dark mood. Not only does Saw brilliantly tell a story of duality and darkness, but it also explores themes of division and identity in modern society. Superb performances from Lupita Nyong'o and Vincent Cassel bring depth and intensity to every scene. Despite some twists in the plot, "Us" makes us think about our dark sides and fears. This film is not only a good horror film, but also a necessary work of art that provokes discussion and opens eyes to the deepest secrets of human nature.

Howard Lois Kelly-Miller Jahnni St. John Richard Clarke Bill Parrish has it all - success, wealth and power. But will he regret his choice when Joe unexpectedly falls in love with Bill's beautiful daughter Susan? Bardzo uroczy film. Niczego mu nie brakuje, mogę uznać go za jeden z moich ulubionych. Skłania do refleksji nad znaczeniem życia a za razem uspokaja że wszystko będzie dobrze. a good movie about love, life and death, it was nice to watch the main character get used to our world and emotions I am absolutely astoneshed and amazed by such a limited and blind percepsion of the people who gave low rate for this movie. This movie is absolutely one of the greatest piece of magic art ever **** you truly have a passion for movies,and wondering about the magic that actors have to bring , then you'll see the highest skills of Bradd Pitt manifesting the first "in flesh" experience of that extraterestrial being wich BY THE WAY  IT IS NOT JUST DEATH .This is what some people don't understand.When "death'' presented himself he mentioned couple of elements or so .... come on people....this movie couldn't be made better than **** english is limited to exprim how high quality this movie has. One of the greatest movie that ive ever seen. I see many reviewers said that this movie is slow but i think they are unprofessional reviewers who didnt have the ability, time, and patience to enjoy a masterpiece like this, to feel the meaning of the value of love, family, death, sacrifices, ... that the film want to convey. This is absolute cinema!. Highly recommend. Finally, my advice for people who is in a desperation: "If you want to die, dont keel yourself but meet Joe Black" The cast's performance is very good. So are the camera and scenery. I can grant the story many licences; like death being a creature (when in fact is a process). The reason why I am torpedoing the rating is the bad morals this movie conveys through Joe Black. Being him Death itself, one would have expected him to have a wisdom nurtured through millenia capable of seeing love as more than getting into the bedroom of a woman. Were Death a creature, his capacity to contemplate beauty should go far beyond drooling over a pair of breasts and a tight butt, it should be able to contemplate the person's soul. There are some things between a man and a woman that can only happen within marriage, and Joe Black should have known that after seeing millions of souls going either to Heaven or to Hell. An intriguing premise; death coming to meet his victim before sweeping him away. Anthony Hopkins is wonderful, as ever. Worth watching just for his understated yet compelling performance. If you skip the scenes with Brad Pitt in, you'd have a great film. Meet Joe Black. Taxes and death. Quite an unusual story and excellent acting. Brad Pitt and his character Joe Black deserve special praise, who often changes from a sweet and funny guy to a harsh, cold and insensitive person. I have a habit, which makes me waste a lot of time, I don't leave a movie unfinished, it can be the biggest crap, I must stay until the end. this was the case with this garbage I came across, unfortunately, today.
The film is so lame, it impressed me, I was laughing, it seems comedy, it actually seems ironic, how ridiculous it is.
but I'm not even going to devote much time to talking about the film, I'm just going to mention some of the countless nonsense. first, the old man to whom "death" ascribes some dignity, is simply a mediocre, idiot, stupid, unhappy old man. this old man is portrayed as a hero in the film, he is a "good man", who according to death goes to paradise, like a good Christian.
the most bizarre thing is that the moral of the movie is that money doesn't buy happiness, but the movie just preaches the values ​​of luxury all the time, the hero is the old man who won in life and is **** rich, there is not a single black character, or poor, in the script.
another bizarre point is that the film preaches the lie all the time, note that no one (not even death) is able to tell the reality lol kkkkkk. each one is lying to the other, as if it were perfectly plausible.
I'm really going to think 20 times before I see an American movie again.
North American culture is the most despicable on planet earth, there's no way!!! Quite possibly the "first-draft-iest" movie I've ever seen, if there were such a superlative, "Meet Joe Black" has some terrific ideas in it, but it's all nearly done away with in favor of flowery dialogue, non-essential narrative excess and a muddling of character. This is an odd movie for me to talk about, as I've always found its concept fascinating. I've also been clinically unable to unearth it from the old, never-ending backlog of movies I have to see. Until now, that is. This in mind, though, I don't think I would have expected this movie to be about what it's actually about, preconceived notions notwithstanding. Without giving away too much, there's a tremendously awkward, clunky and at times troubling dynamic involving how Brad Pitt's "Death" comes to be corporeal. I just could not get on board with the idea, even with the satisfying manner in which it comes to an end. As briefly alluded to up top, this movie's runtime is nearly unforgivable. It's three hours long. It did not need to be three hours long. Cut something. I'm looking at you, unnecessary corporate shenanigans subplot. That said, the score for this is quite simply some of the best music you'll probably ever hear in a movie, regardless of the fact that the accompanying images hold little to no weight for at least 85% of the runtime. If you ever wanted to hear a composer work his proverbial ass off to make a movie a seem more interesting, take a listen to what Thomas Newman's done here. It's sublime. All in all, "Meet Joe Black" means well and is handsomely crafted, but I just felt unquestionably distant from the highfalutin nature of it all. Very good movie, didn't realise how long it was until the I saw the time at the end but I wouldn't remove any scene. 760.title: Dredd

760.rich_text:
Dredd Dredd Judgement is coming. Action Science Fiction Pete Travis Karl Urban Olivia Thirlby Lena Headey Wood Harris Langley Kirkwood Tamer Burjaq Joe Vaz Rakie Ayola Junior Singo Luke Tyler In the future, America is a dystopian wasteland. The latest scourge is Ma-Ma, a prostitute-turned-drug pusher with a dangerous new drug and aims to take over the city. The only possibility of stopping her is an elite group of urban police called Judges, who combine the duties of judge, jury and executioner to deliver a brutal brand of swift justice. But even the top-ranking Judge, Dredd, discovers that taking down Ma-Ma isn’t as easy as it seems in this explosive adaptation of the hugely popular comic series. Wait, what?! That's it?! Where's the rest of it? For a 1h 30m film, this holds up extremely well. Every aspect of this film is high quality, well-written, and well-thought-out.

And now you're telling me there is no sequel? WTF?!

For the first 10 minutes of this film, I immediately wanted a Second Film, and by the end, I knew it needed one.

Now, in a technical sense, I should rate this a 10/10; however, due to its short Run Time, the film has no time to keep the wheels turning. It ends without saying anything more, not even explaining anything; it just ends.

Why? Lionsgate, we need the Sequel. I want to see Anderson and Dredd up against another day of crime in Mega City One.

If you can make 59 John Wick films, then you can fund a sequel to this 8/10 film, which is a 10/10 masterpiece.

The Artistic feel and grimness of this film are unlike anything else in the film industry.
If you haven't watched this film, you need to see it and pray that we get another one more than a Decade later.

If the Sequel, whenever we get it, is even better than this one and is a continuation of the storyline of Dredd and Anderson, I will have to raise the score of this film by one.

8/10, I love this, I want more, **** I'll even see it in theatres. A straight shot of the 2000AD comic that I loved from start to finish!  Karl Urban nails the tone and tenor even if he's not as big but this was a hit for me and I can't say enough about Heady as Maw-Maw!  BANG! Dredd knows exactly what it is: a short and fun movie, with good characters and great visuals.

The characters are not layered too much, but they have enough satisfying backstory elements and some characteristics that make me care for them. The story is simple and straightforward, but effective because of the character and the world building. The world feels lived in and quite realistic compared to other some other cyberpunk sci-fi films. On the negative side, I thought the villain was extremely one dimensional. The dialogues are simple, but mostly good with some lines that come back for a second time.

The directing is great, it's clear what this movie wants to achieve. The cinematography is outstanding with the amazig slow-motion sequences and the POVs. This movie looks digital, but in a good way, because it's futuristic and unique at the same time. The production design, color grading and visual effects create that look and I'm here to love it. The score is also unique and amazing, but not something that I'd listen to outside of the film. The cast is good and the acting is convincing.

Dredd is straightforward and so much fun. 10/10 no notes. One of the best comic-based movies of all time. Fast paced, brutal, entertaining, great cast.. It's like a superhero version of The Raid but with guns and gore.
I am taking a point off because the CGI hasn't aged that well. it's one of those movies that's objectively a solid 7 out of 10, but purely for the entertainment value you get out of it, it's an 11. This film belongs on the Mount Rushmore of comic book movies. i mean come on did you see how well Karl Urban does the mouth thing? Dredd is dark, gritty and exciting brought to big screen experience that delivers on all of the notes it needs to. Having Karl Urban portray Dredd was a very very welcome addition despite the uncertainty to the decision. The film delivered on all of the aspects a Dredd film should; Gratuitous violence of the 80's, dark almost depressing atmosphere, subtle tensions around biases and most important of all a too cool for it's own good attitude that seems out of place in the 20 something's but not in the 1980 something era it clearly emulates. The film also did not suffer from the horrific decision of deciding to have Dredd unmask himself based entirely around having a big name actor have his face seen. Almost as if making a point of avoiding this decision the films shows Dredd's silhouette without his helmet and shows him front and center placing it on his head and makes a clear point of never taking it off. Dredd isn't shown like the 95 film to be infallible in a fight and this film as if to avoid this goes out of it's way to display to the viewer that like anyone Dredd is another man, just highly self-sufficient. This film couldn't go more of a different direction than the 95 version. What 1995 gets wrong about Dredd this film gets absolutely right but where this film falls over is in it's depiction of the rule of law and Mega-City One as a whole. In the comics the depiction of Mega-City one is that it is complete dystopian, authoritarian rule of law, for gods sake in the comics littering is a five year sentence in the ice-cubes. The depiction of Mega-City One should not be grimy and gritty because that's not the city itself but rather the underworld of the city. The way Mega-City One is actually supposed to be depicted is as a clean and totally safe city so long as the law is followed and not having this aspect in this film was a rather large point deduction. The film does well to capture the general movie goer and casual fan of the series, more die-hard fans and hardliners are going to be mixed or generally favourable rather than absolutely positive. Another attempt with more passion for the franchise would be very very welcome, however unlikely it is. Great effects. Urban is perfect as Dredd. Gritty and atmospheric. Quick watch at 90 odd minutes. One of the best comic book adaptations. Oublié, anéanti, le pathétique film avec Stallone ! le vrai juge Dredd, c’est "Dredd" ! Ce juge Dredd là est le meilleur film d’action depuis Robocop, le tout premier Robocop. Une ambiance similaire, un personnage raide comme la justice, draconien, un homme d’honneur. 

Dans ce monde un brin madmaxien (aussi), le juge fait le grand ménage par le **** éradique les cafards et autres crevures avec un aplomb qui ravit le spectateur. Et il a la classe. Il est accompagné d’une recrue aux cheveux jaunes, télépathe, qui donne un heureux contrepoids à son impavidité. Un duo particulièrement **** rythme est très soutenu, la réalisation est excellente, pas de cut & move ici, pas de montage pourri à la Bourne. 

Entre quelques ralentis à 300 im/s et de l’image de synthèse utilisée à très bon escient, c’est un boulot d’artisan, Verhoeven serait fier de ce réalisateur inconnu au bataillon mais très consciencieux.

Aucune star à 20 millions de dollars ici, juste des acteurs et actrices au service du film, au service de leur rôle comme Karl Urban et Lena Headey. C’est sobre et très efficace. La musique électro endiablée est également fort réussie et sert l’action avec brio. 

Bref, je suis sur le cul ! cette licence a (enfin) retrouvé ses lettres de noblesse. Comme quoi tout arrive ! Great action-filled movie but with a sub-par plot and dialogues.  Unfortunately not as great as the original. The setting, pulp, and camp are all operating at full efficiency here, wish the action and story could of kept up a little better but I enjoyed it.
