819.title: Speak No Evil

metadata.tagline: Hear no evil.

819.rich_text: Speak No Evil Speak No Evil Hear no evil. Horror Thriller James Watkins James McAvoy Mackenzie Davis Scoot McNairy Aisling Franciosi Alix West Lefler Dan Hough Kris Hitchen Motaz Malhees Jakob Højlev Jørgensen When an American family is invited to spend the weekend at the idyllic country estate of a charming British family they befriended on vacation, what begins as a dream holiday soon warps into a snarled psychological nightmare. The movie was not very good. It follows a nice family visiting another that turns out to be extremely irritating. Most of the film focuses on that dynamic, which quickly becomes dull. The eventual twist reveals that the hosts intend to murder their guests and take their belongings. The earlier emphasis on their annoying behavior feels unrelated to that motive, as if the story shifted direction partway through production. As usual it's the European white rural persona which is to be associated with evil. Make no mistake, this is not coincidental. Fascinante, cruel, sombrio. Daqueles filmes que a gente termina totalmente estarrecido, chocado e atônito. Christian Tafdrup's 2022 film Speak No Evil is not a horror film. It's more of a thriller about a murderous married couple, but it lacks any kind of thrill. While Christian Tafdrup has attempted to build the tension slowly and culminate in a terrifying finale, the story's construction is at times rather inconclusive. From the very beginning, the characters Bjorn and Luise are presented as sacrificial lambs, with whom anything can be done, making them easy prey for the questionable behavior of their hosts. Bjorn, in particular, is reduced to an incapacitated idiot who allows himself to be pushed around and killed by a madman. The true motivation for the murder(s) also remains unclear. The characterization of the main characters ruins the good idea of ​​a film that lacks a believable plot. More thriller drama than horror, so disappointed from that point of view, but otherwise a pretty good movie. Suspense until the end. This remake of a 2022 Danish film of the same name sees an American couple (McKenzie Davis and Scoot McNairy) vacationing in Italy with their daughter where they meet a seemingly friendly and charming British couple (James McAvoy and Aisling Franciosi) who invite them to stay in their remote country home. Things become clearer and clearer that the couple have sinister intentions for their guests and are not who they seem to be. For starters, the previews of this one, coupled with the fact that it's a remake of an already pretty recent film didn't really have me sold on this one initially. I did find myself slightly intrigued by the prospect of seeing McAvoy in another dark role following his career-best turn in the M. Night Shyamalan films 'Split' and 'Glass'. After hearing surprisingly good things, I figured I'd give it a go. The result is not too tense and eerie, with not a whole lot of suspense or buildup. However, it hardly matters here, and McAvoy is in beast mode once again here. He's the film's real draw. Otherwise, it plays out about how one might expect. Overall, predictable and not too suspenseful, but McAvoy really needs to keep playing and taking on roles like this, cause he kills it every time (no pun intended). Remake de um filme dinamarquês, curti muito a pegada de suspense, por mais que o terror do filme demore a pegar, é extremamente eficiente em criar o clima de tensão, mesmo com algumas piadas exageradas. A família tradicional é posta ali em espelho aos seus medos pequeno-burgueses, como as regras de etiqueta, de linguagem, do sexo, e tudo isso é explorado de modo às vezes hilário. Quando o terror começa, a cena onde se descobre estarem presos para o abate é digna de provocar calafrios, e a aprtir daí a tensão só aumenta, por mais que, novamente, tenha exageros dignos de filmes pastelão. O final é arrebatador, não poupando sangue. Filme pipoca muito bom, com uma refilmagem bem vinda. Although Speak No Evil doesn't delve into deeper issues, the cast's performances and the overall narrative direction remain solid, successfully creating a deeply unsettling weekend experience. A lot of people and a lot of these reviews did not understand the movie at all. There are no plot holes aside from the general "I would not do this if it were me". Everything makes sense and the point that the movie doesn't not beat you over the head with was very clear if you are not simple Too many plot conveniences to take it seriously. Still, the tension from so many uncomfortable moments is worth watching. And I didn't expect that bleak ending. Not your standard Hollywood cookie cutter horror. Great cinematography, acting, takes its time to build the tension.

820.title: The Witch

metadata.tagline: Evil takes many forms.

820.rich_text:
The Witch The Witch Evil takes many forms. Horror Fantasy Drama Robert Eggers Anya Taylor-Joy Ralph Ineson Kate Dickie Harvey Scrimshaw Ellie Grainger Lucas Dawson Julian Richings Bathsheba Garnett Sarah Stephens Daniel Malik In 1630, a farmer relocates his family to a remote plot of land on the edge of a forest where strange, unsettling things happen. With suspicion and paranoia mounting, each family member's faith, loyalty and love are tested in shocking ways. The Witch is not my kind of film, but boy is it well made!

I love that I only understood at the end what the whole movie was about: Satan slowly manipulated the whole family and made them be suspicious of each other. He picked one person who he drove crazy in order to recruit her as a witch. I love when an ending gives a new meaning to the story. The characters are very well-written, just like the dialogues.

The cinematography is really good with natural lighting and slow camera movements, but this was just the start for Robert Eggers, his style gets better from here. The score is great and fits the era. The sound is perfect. There were times I thought those sounds were in my home, it was so creepy I had to take my earphones out to check. The cast is great and the acting performances are perfect. It's always great to hear Ralph Ineson speak and Anya Taylor-Joy is terrific.

The Witch is the kind of horror that's far from my taste, but it's so well-made, that I can't stop praising it. the film is interesting in terms of atmosphere and shots, the plot leaves a lot unsaid, how did it happen at the end?, what was that?, the film doesn't tell a lot and you have to guess and it was terrifying The Witch" (2015) is a chilling and atmospheric horror film that breathes new life into the genre with its fresh perspective and unsettling exploration of religious paranoia and folklore. This film is not your typical jump-scare fest; it's a slow-burn descent into madness that will leave you disturbed and captivated long after the credits **** in 17th-century New England, the film follows a Puritan family exiled from their community and forced to confront the dark forces lurking in the surrounding wilderness. The film masterfully creates a sense of isolation and dread, immersing you in the family's paranoia and the chilling atmosphere of the **** performances are exceptional, with Anya Taylor-Joy delivering a breakout performance as Thomasin, the eldest daughter accused of witchcraft. The supporting cast is equally impressive, capturing the religious fervor and growing hysteria of the family as they succumb to fear and **** film's cinematography is stunning, with its stark visuals and haunting landscapes creating a sense of unease and isolation. The sound design is equally effective, with its eerie silence punctuated by unsettling sounds and chilling whispers."The Witch" is a must-watch for horror fans seeking a truly unique and disturbing experience. Its fresh perspective on the genre, combined with its masterful execution and haunting atmosphere, make it a modern horror masterpiece. This is one of the most rare, powerful films I've ever seen.  It doesn't feel like a movie, it feels like a window into a different time.  Eggers is an immaculate director and brings this vision to life in a way most filmmakers would envy. Decent spooky flick. Bit of a slow burn with with a couple very creepy scenes that will stick in my head.
Was let down by the cinematography after seeing the Northman first and having high expectations. Found some of the low light scenes to be decent however lighting wise. Overall similar to Asters films it is a fresh take on horror but not sure what it is trying to say in terms of themes or overall message (if there is one) Feral and unrelenting.  A darkly imaginative fable that seems simultaneously all too real and a part of some religious fanatic's fevered nightmare.  The cast of recognizable actors disappear so thoroughly into their roles that they could have been plucked from the colonies themselves. A terrifying film with an unapologetic take on the foolishness of religion and superstition. Anya Taylor-Joy is a joy to watch (no pun intended), but Ralph Ineson takes the crown with his incredible voice. You may know him from the Diablo 4 trailer. This film slogged along, never becoming interesting.  If this is horror, then Ghostbusters is a romantic drama.There's little engaging about this movie.  I watched the film, just waiting and waiting for something interesting to happen.  As it turns out, a movie about speculation isn't all that interesting. Even better on the second viewing. I didn't like the ending first time around, and I don't know what I was thinking because it fits perfectly. I dig folklore, I dig history, and I dig beautiful cinematography (This is a digitally shot film?!). So many ways to watch this and so many layers to the characters, a lot of Freud and Kubrick, and amazing child actors! Great vibes and I could of honestly done with double the amount of screen time for the witch and the scares. Would not mind a black Phillip extended universe.

821.title: The Woman in Cabin 10

metadata.tagline: They don't want you to believe what she saw.

821.rich_text: The Woman in Cabin 10 The Woman in Cabin 10 They don't want you to believe what she saw. Mystery Thriller Crime Simon Stone Keira Knightley Guy Pearce David Ajala Gitte Witt Art Malik Gugu Mbatha-Raw Hannah Waddingham Kaya Scodelario David Morrissey Daniel Ings On a lavish yacht for an assignment, a journalist sees a passenger go overboard. But when no one believes her, she risks her life to uncover the truth. A movie has got to have something, and this has nothing. The most straightforward and safe 'mystery' I can remember in a long time. The Woman in Cabin 10 doesn’t try to reinvent the genre, but it knows exactly what it wants to be — a sleek, fast-paced psychological thriller that gets straight to the point. From the very first scene, it dives into the story without wasting time on endless introductions or forced exposition. That alone is refreshing in a sea of overcomplicated mysteries.Keira Knightley carries the film with confidence. Her character —a slightly unstable journalist who witnesses (or thinks she witnesses) a murder aboard a luxury yacht— moves between paranoia and lucidity with the grace we expect from her. She’s the glue that keeps everything together, even when the script starts to wobble.Visually, it’s elegant. The direction makes smart use of confined spaces, mirrors, and the oppressive calm of the open sea. It builds that sense of isolation and doubt where everyone hides something and truth becomes slippery. There are hints of Hitchcock, though without his finesse, and a touch of whodunnit style polished for the Netflix era: glossy, pretty, and a bit ****’s enjoyable, if not memorable. The film delivers decent tension and solid craftsmanship, though the mystery resolves too neatly. It feels like it could have gone deeper — into its characters, or into the unease it hints at but never fully embraces.Still, I never got bored. The Woman in Cabin 10 is the kind of polished thriller that works perfectly for a quiet night: engaging, well-made, and just mysterious enough to keep you watching until the very end. A very mediocre mystery that wastes a talented cast on a plot that we've been through hundreds of times before. Comienza algo lenta después mejora el ritmo, me resultó entretenida para pasar el rato, pero es predecible, La obsesión de la protagonista con el misterio es muy exagerado y poco creíble. An almost instantly forgettable film with an appalling script.  The ending in particular was terrible! That said, some of the acting was decent enough, and it flowed quite well, until the end!!! I wouldn't bother watching it again! This was disappointing. Did the producers, Director, and cast and crew not realize how bad this was while filming? Kiera Knightly will find it difficult to get jobs after this horrific performance. I’ve seen Hallmark and Lifetime movies with a better score and overall better production! The supporting actors were given too much weight to carry for the Lead by KK! They tried! Simon Stone certainly tried to create a vivid thriller. But it's clear from the start that it wasn't made to satisfy any high expectations. The script is too weak and riddled with far too many illogical sequences. This is probably also due to the novel by Ruth Ware on which it is based. The characters are as superficial as the story, which prevents any truly convincing tension from building. All in all, it's a film you can watch to pass the time, but one you shouldn't have too high expectations for. Great oldskool thriller! Top cast and scenery. It might be “bon ton” for critics  these days to completely tear down 95% of the films they review  -the best sailors stand on shore, right?- but this definitely a movie worth watching. Enjoy! Is this a cinematic masterpiece? Definitely not. I thought it was good enough (and short enough) to sit through once though. The mystery aspect of the story is dropped halfway through, but I actually didn't mind that. And the ending was decently satisfying. The story is incredibly simple, which can sometimes be refreshing, but it's up to you what you want out of a mystery movie. A murder mystery on a luxurious yacht. What could go wrong? The script! I had high hopes for this film, but unfortunately, it's a shallow thriller that stops being interesting about halfway through. I mean it when I say it's shallow—absolutely no character gets any kind of background story, nor do they make you wish for one. It's a "whodunit" movie where the mystery is solved too early and in a very unsatisfactory way. The film is already quite short, but maybe you should just watch the trailer, it's more interesting.

822.rich_text:
From Paris with Love From Paris with Love Two agents. One city. No merci. Action Crime Thriller Pierre Morel John Travolta Jonathan Rhys Meyers Kasia Smutniak Richard Durden Bing Yin Amber Rose Revah Éric Godon François Bredon Chems Dahmani Sami Darr James Reese has a good job as an ambassador's aid in France, but his real passion is a side gig—working in a minor role in the CIA. He would love to be a full-fledged agent and can't believe his luck when he lands an assignment with Charlie Wax. Trigger-happy Charlie soon has James crying for his desk job, but when he learns that the same guys they're trying to catch are after him, James realises that Charlie may be his only hope of survival. A film with a classic plot but a pleasant narrative pace (a fast-paced plot that avoids being boring and repetitive) and stands out from others of its genre for its irony, which is a key aspect of the film. It lasts just the right amount of time. I didn't think that it would be such a good action movie, for action movies the main problem is the length with which the action hangs, but in this film the running time is enough to show the different culture of the city, shootouts, jokes and a love story, the film is short but contains everything that makes it a great film, the main characters are charismatic and work well in contrast, I recommend it to everyone From Paris with Love is a typical French crime thriller. Most of the film is an action scene, which is not bad for a French film. John Travolta's good acting. In general, when watching a movie, it feels like you're watching an American movie. In general, as the thriller From Paris with Love falls apart around the middle of the story, it's more of a linear action movie. And as From Paris with Love is not bad, there is no suspense here. The finale is disappointing, it is mediocre even for films of this genre. From Paris with Love can be watched once in the evening and safely forgotten the next morning. For a mindless action flick, it was incredibly accurate to how terrorist cells operated in Iraq/Afghanistan when the sht was hot in the 2000s, speaking from personal experience. It takes a dump on women and racial minorities but it's too **** netwoks, the bomb making cells, the drugs to fund the terrorist schemes, the ideology, etc. It's also a good reference to the Royal With Cheese. Cheesey cliche chess start scene, because every one who plays chess must be intelligent and tactical right?
- Awfully unrealistic gun and hand to hand combat scenes.
- John Travolta kills people on whims. Why is he not in jail.
- What motive does his caucasian girlfriend have to suicide bomb some conference.
The reason it isn't a 1 is because I quite enjoyed Jonathan Rhys Meyers and John Travoltas bromance throughout. From Paris With Love was an entertaining ride, with plenty of "edge of your seat" moments, humor, and lots of action. The plot kept twisting and turning, bringing one surprise after the other, which made it really interesting. Travolta was dynamic, fun and believable as a seemingly crazy but very able operative/spy. Jonathan Rhys Meyers was excellent in the role of the newbie operative who was fairly innocent and very inexperienced, but still smart. It was a far cry from the authority and power he exudes as King Henry in the Tudors series, which means to me that he's a capable actor. From Paris With Love plays as though it were the fourth or fifth sequel in a legendary saga, that has reached it's end and is just milking another film out of the story. It's adequate and somewhat entertaining, but nowhere near as good as it should have been. Jonathan Rhys-Meyers stars a a junior C.I.A. agent, working out of the U.S. Embassy in Paris. Until now he's been asked to do simple things. His role quickly changes once and international terror cell sets up shop in his backyard. Rhys-Meyers is quickly paired with a veteran C.I.A. hit-man. The kind of guy you call when you want things done quickly and under the radar, but years of killing has taken it's toll. The mysterious man has become cold and reckless to a fault. The story here is painfully predictable, in a film that is about half as long as it should have been. Yes, the film is basically non-stop action, but it moves in such a way that the story is rushed to the point of confusion. Jonathan Rhys-Meyers was terrific in an opposites attract kind of way. John Travolta on the other hand was much too old and out of shape to be believable as this crazy, over the top hit-man. The chemistry between the two and the amazing non-stop action make this movie a pretty entertaining one, but the predictability and rushed story take too much away to make it the kind of film that keeps audiences buzzing after it's over. Whilst it's not exactly high art, From Paris with Love is a very entertaining slice of popcorn action. John Travolta is excellent as the maniacal agent Wax; he's just tons of fun to watch. Well paced with exciting action scenes, From Paris with Love is a superior action flick. Great action movie. Need more of this nowadays. Travolta is great. As well as Rhys Meyers. They make a good pair. The movie is not too long and full of action.  Overall this one reminded me of "Shoot 'Em Up" with Clive Owen. There is little left to the imagination when most of the posters promoting ‘From Paris with Love’ show a bald and bearded John Travolta holding a rocket launcher, we now know exactly what we are in for, an over the top and ridiculous 90 **** man is it enjoyable.
Jonathan Rys Meyers stars as James Reese, a small time CIA operative who sights are higher within the place, but who is also a personal aide to a US Ambassador for France, and he’s quite good at his job, and of course he has the woman of his dreams, but when his wish for a more responsible role within the CIA comes to life in the form of unorthodox operative Charlie Wax, played by John Travolta, it isn’t exactly what James was expecting, especially when a shootout goes awry and he ends up carrying a vase full of cocaine around for quite a bit of the film.
John Travolta is without doubt the best thing about the film, his absurd characteristics of Charlie Wax, drinking mint tea, lunch on the Eiffel Tower and being in love with his ‘wife’, a gun, are hysterical, but he also proves he can play the bad guy with excellent effect, alongside the calmer Meyers.While the legendary actor has had his ups and downs across the years, he has proven himself as quite a diverse actor, particularly in his action oriented turns in this and The taking of Pelham 123. Meyers often portrays very serious and one dimensional characters, but again he seems to be enjoying himself throughout the movie, the mismatch of leading actors certainly paid off as is proven by the surprising chemistry of the level-headed James Reese and the crazy Charlie Wax.
The writing certainly has its spark in moments, but this is very much a popcorn flick with plenty of brawling in the most unorthodox of circumstances and enough firepower to keep the bloodthirsty fans amused, it is what A Good Day to Die Hard should have been.
From Paris with Love rightly prides itself in its absurdity, whether its hiding various weapon parts in energy drinks to get through airport customs, hanging out of a speeding car with a rocket launcher or the unbelievable plot which takes each and every twist and turn imaginable, it all equals out to an enjoyable flick that is easy on the eyes but not so much on the ears.

This movie is a remake of a 1979 horror classic, which most people no longer know. A character chasing life is one of the more overwhelmingly hurtful but truthful things you could possibly watch or relate to. Ben Stiller reaches into the hearts and minds of his watchers with this one. 
The film follows a man, Walter Mitty, and his seemingly lowly and slow-paced life. He's a by-the-rulebook man slowly drawn further and further out of his comfort zone in this play on 'Man's Search for Meaning'.

warm film about a hardworking and responsible person An amazing movie with lots of message. Full and rich. Wonder those professional critics have watch it at all. The rare case of a maligned remake, a long-term resident of development hell, which seems to have benefited from extended incubation. As the offbeat saga of a chronic introvert, so conflicted he debates the merits of a single mouse click, The Secret Life of Walter Mitty thrives on its spirited imagination and the audience's uncertainty about where the line stretches between stark reality and vibrant make-believe. These scenes, peppered with equal amounts of breakneck effects magic and surprising, effective laughs, are the heart and soul of the movie. Not only do they keep the pace skipping along at a frantic speed, but they also effectively foreshadow upcoming events, convey Walter's wants and needs, and chart his progress on the road to self-discovery.

Ben Stiller is wonderful in the leading role, both as a mousey, zoned-out ghost at the journey's outset and the large, confident individual he becomes, and the awkward chemistry he shares with Kristen Wiig is just right. My sole complaint, really, is that after handling so much in the opening acts, it feels stuck during the slower-paced home stretch. Intelligent, thoughtful, entertaining adventures - both real and imagined - with a beating heart and a fresh sense of style. In regards to any review before.

Men in Black II Men in Black II Same planet. New scum. Action Comedy Science Fiction Barry Sonnenfeld Tommy Lee Jones Will Smith Rip Torn Lara Flynn Boyle Johnny Knoxville Rosario Dawson Tony Shalhoub Patrick Warburton Jack Kehler David Cross Kay and Jay reunite to provide our best, last and only line of defense against a sinister seductress who levels the toughest challenge yet to the MIB's untarnished mission statement – protecting Earth from the scum of the universe. It's been four years since the alien-seeking agents averted an intergalactic disaster of epic proportions. Now it's a race against the clock as Jay must convince Kay – who not only has absolutely no memory of his time spent with the MIB, but is also the only living person left with the expertise to save the galaxy – to reunite with the MIB before the earth submits to ultimate destruction. The fading luster **** franchise: A 3.0-star sequel stuck in a cosmic loop.2012 (3.0)I watched "Men in Black II" in 2012, and it felt like a decent but somewhat uninspired continuation of the high-tension original. While the first film was a "sensational" breakthrough in the sci-fi comedy genre, this 2002 sequel struggled to recapture that same "raw" magic ten years after its initial release. The "chewy" chemistry between Will Smith and Tommy Lee Jones was still present, providing a comfortable rhythm, but the plot felt like a familiar rehash of tropes rather than a fresh "revelation." The alien designs were imaginative, yet the storytelling lacked the visceral edge that usually keeps me fully immersed in a 4.0-star or 5.0-star experience. With 95% preservation of my memory, I recall enjoying the lighthearted gags and the fast-paced action, but the overall depth was missing, leaving me in a state of mild satisfaction rather than true excitement. It wasn't a "1.0-star trauma" like some of the hollow fantasies I've encountered, but it didn't possess the intellectual weight or the daring subversion of a masterpiece like "Chronicle." It stands in my archive as a solid 3.0-star viewing—a nostalgic but safe journey that offered a bit of fun without ever truly breaking the fourth wall or challenging my expectations of what a sci-fi sequel could be. This is nowhere near as memorable as the first film, if this had been the first film then I don’t think they would have made any more. Strangely the music doesn’t always feel appropriate for the scene and is too often out-of-place. The special effects are worse, especially the worm subway opening debacle. They only had one joke throughout, which was to wipe someone’s memory and then make up a stupid new one. It passes the time and isn’t totally bad, there are some entertaining moments that just about offset all the bad bits to make this very average. The story is quite badly written, it’s just a rehash of the first film but with the first half dedicated to resetting the previous ending. I’m making a bold prediction that it’s not worth watching past the first film. Good movie, funny at times, great visuals at times, but the first was better. Storyline was o.k. but nothing too special. Plot that wants to be more developed than the previous film but without much success. The dose of irony present in the first film remains, even if slightly less effective Will abimizin yapımları hoşuma gider ama bu yapımın ortalama bir yapım olduğu gerçeğini değiştirmiyor. Günümüz izleyicinin beğenmeme olasılığı yüksek. An extraterrestrial menace, once thought neutralized, returns to Earth and threatens the planet. Predictably, this draws the interest of the Men in Black, but as the case is so old, none of the current agents know how to handle it. Cue the mothballed Agent K (Tommy Lee Jones), who’s collected from a mind-wiped retirement and reunited with his old suit, gizmos and memories. K’s return sits well with Agent J (Will Smith), as he’s been struggling to train a suitable replacement since his mentor’s untimely departure at the end of the first film.

Harmless but toothless, MiB2 replays the hits but lacks the careful balance and memorable secondary charms that made the original so effective. Running short on fun little bits like the opening confrontation at the Mexican border or the baby delivery scene, the sequel is more flat and businesslike. As K is now secure in his role as an unflappable field agent, the film misses his dazzled rookie’s perspective; someone to gape and goggle at all the weird shapes and colors wriggling under the noses of oblivious New Yorkers. Rosario Dawson’s character is a flimsy effort to replicate that. She plays an adorably doe-eyed pizza waitress who witnesses an alien hold-up, but after a flirty first encounter with the agency, she’s shuffled off screen and forgotten until the climax.

No one should’ve expected a villainous performance on par with Vincent D’Onofrio’s man-skinned cockroach, but Lara Flynn Boyle’s tentacled space queen is still a major step down. She’s all unwarranted arrogance and cold sex appeal, a stuffy foil who waves unconvincing green CG appendages in lieu of a more distinct personality. I’m not sure Famke Janssen would’ve been better in the role, as originally cast, but she can’t have been much worse. The best thing I can say about Boyle is that she adequately fills out the skimpy lingerie she’s inherited from the wardrobe department.

Comparisons to a franchise’s first outing are rarely favorable to the sequel. Such is the case, across the board, for Men in Black II. Most of the best jokes fall before the law of diminishing returns, a long preamble hinders Jones and Smith’s efforts to recapture the magic of their first pairing, and the light primary storyline is a case more befitting of the Saturday morning cartoon files than the big screen. 828.rich_text:
Ghostbusters: Afterlife Ghostbusters: Afterlife Discover the past. Save the future. Fantasy Comedy Adventure Jason Reitman Mckenna Grace Finn Wolfhard Carrie Coon Bokeem Woodbine Paul Rudd Logan Kim Celeste O'Connor Bill Murray Dan Aykroyd Ernie Hudson When single mom Callie and her two kids Trevor and Phoebe arrive in a small Oklahoma town, they begin to discover their connection to the original Ghostbusters and the secret legacy their grandfather left behind. Ghostbusters: Afterlife has again like Frozen Empire it's good and bad bits as it relives a bit and passes on to the new generation but you are in for the most bumpy ride you will ever see!. Business dried up quickly for the original Ghostbusters, after their fateful 1984 duel with Gozer the Gozerian halted all the paranormal phenomena that made their jobs necessary. Too good for their own good, in other words, and after the money ran out, the team splintered to pursue their own next chapters. All except Egon, that is, who remained convinced of a looming sinister spook until the day he died. Now, in the midst of sorting through his estate, the brainy buster's grown daughter and grandkids are digging through his old toys, unraveling that mystery and getting in way over their heads.

Afterlife is a film that tries extra-hard to pluck the strings of nostalgia and works overtime to surround us with the fresh, quirky character that made the first Ghostbusters so unforgettable... sometimes to its own detriment. Although the three remaining original heroes only stop by for a word or two, the shadows of their past selves loom tall and large, regularly outshining the mousier, more introverted comedic stylings of the new players. It's wonderful to hear so many familiar cues in the musical score (great call there), to inspect old props and clips and memories from new angles, to see how the exploits of this fab four are regarded by the public forty years later, but at some point we need to move on, to fill the void with something fresh, and I don't think this gets us there. The kids do well with the material, but they're not really distinct or vibrant enough to carry the load by themselves. Paul Rudd makes for a fine supporting player, lands a number of the film's best laughs, but he's inessential, disappearing for long stretches of time. The scale of the story is very small, too, despite its boasts **** peril, and the action is kept equally low-key.

Still, it's not bad. Afterlife has loads of bright ideas and its heart's in the right place. The humor works, though it's in a different vein than the forebearer it so clearly idolizes, and the adept mix of CG and practical effects perform very well. As an homage, it serves the purpose. 832.rich_text:
The Rock The Rock Alcatraz. Only one man has ever broken out. Now five million lives depend on two men breaking in. Action Adventure Thriller Michael Bay Sean Connery Nicolas Cage Ed Harris John Spencer David Morse William Forsythe Michael Biehn Vanessa Marcil John C. McGinley Gregory Sporleder When vengeful General Francis X. Hummel seizes control of Alcatraz Island and threatens to launch missiles loaded with deadly chemical weapons into San Francisco, only a young FBI chemical weapons expert and notorious Federal prisoner have the skills to penetrate the impregnable island fortress and take him down. Just a great action thriller with an amazing cast. Keeps you engaged from the start and doesn't let up until the credits roll. Michael Bay is often considered the laughing stock of movie directors, but yet his movies have such style, swagger, and bravado. Often times he is grossly enamored in his own style that the storytelling takes a bit of dive. However, 1996’s The Rock starring Sean Connery and Nicholas Cage is more than likely his greatest film. It combines his unique style of cinematography and action with surprisingly thoughtful writing and storytelling (Mostly because the writers are David Weisberg, Douglas Cook, and Mark Rosner). The action is genuinely enjoyable, the themes of veteran mistreatment, government manipulation, legitimately humorous dialogue that holds up pretty well, and a concept believable enough it doesn’t feel over the top. Alcatraz has in the past been a staging point for a takeover. From 1969-1971 the “Indians of all tribes” saw indigenous people occupy the island in protest of a message. - So not only is the plot of the movie backed by an understandable, and sympathetic motivational driving force it is grounded in some shred of believability which makes it all the more engaging. Furthermore, the motivations of the antagonist characters are understandable considering the gross mistreatment the government does unto veterans, especially those who need treatment the most like those who were injured in the line of duty, prisoners of war, and the families related to those killed in action. It leaves it very morally ambiguous, and to keep this mostly spoiler free, it leaves it relatively so until certain characters become blinded by being overzealous. The weakest characters are the protagonist, but it doesn’t really upset me that much. Cage’s character is very two dimensional and while he does go through a character arc it feels as though he lacks much of a personality. Connery’s character is also two dimensional, but you are drip fed enough information to care about his struggle and badass-ery that you don’t care about it being two dimensional. I will say I prefer his character like this, as nothing ever fully explained or elaborated on which makes it much more unique of a concept for a character. When aspects of a story or a character are left open to interpretation, I find it to be a more unique brand of storytelling. Similar to leaning at the edge of your seat and never getting to rest you back against the chair again, it’s a nice touch. - Lastly, this movie has a fan theory that this is a James Bond sequel, and I do appreciate the theory and it makes rewatching it a whole lot of fun. Really good movie. good movie, but you sympathize with the main villain and empathize with the couple of main characters, the hostages are completely indifferent and the government is very vile and arrogant The Rock (1996) is a solid action-packed ride from start to finish. The plot is straightforward but executed well, with a strong first act that sets everything up nicely. The pacing keeps things moving without dragging, and there's a good balance between intense action and quieter moments that build character relationships. The script is solid, delivering sharp dialogue and a few memorable lines that stick with you long after the credits roll.

Michael Bay’s direction is exactly what you’d expect, high-energy, explosive, and visually dynamic. The cinematography has that gritty yet polished look that works perfectly for this kind of movie, making the action sequences feel immersive and intense. Bay’s signature camera movements and framing give everything a larger-than-life feel, keeping the tension high. The sound design and score are fantastic, elevating the emotional beats and the action without overpowering the scenes.

The performances are a big part of what makes The Rock work so well. Sean Connery has an undeniable screen presence, bringing charisma and weight to his role, while Nicolas Cage delivers a strong performance that balances his character’s intelligence and unpredictability. Ed Harris also stands out, adding depth to a character that could have easily been one-dimensional. With great action sequences, strong performances, and a tight script, The Rock is a top-tier action movie that holds up incredibly well. This second film from Michael bay is his bestband most restrained and thoughtful effort the plot manages to be plausible and making sense and the dialogue is stellar, the performances from top to bottom are first class Sean Connery deserved an Oscar nom for this and Nicolas cage, Ed Harris John Spencer and the rest of the cast are also phenomenal, I cared for everyone in it the action scenes were intelligent and filmed in a way that’s smart and intelligent there was logic to it. It brings something new to the action genre with original charachters that are not cliched and have a strong and compelling personality, you can get invested with what their intentions are and why they are doing it. Just like you want from a Michael bay film the story is very interesting and well written. The direction was astonishing this is high quality filmmaking at its finest better than speed or face off this makes those two films look mediocre in comparison. The rock is just as intelligent an action film as terminator 2, robocop and raiders of the lost ark. It’s easy to comprehend what’s going on within the adventure of it. The final battle was so exciting and the ending was just heartwarming and as it’s dedicated to the late Partner of Jerry bruckheimer don simpson  as they made five awesome and mind blowing blockbuster epics and this final collaboration of them along with crimson tide is there best one a work of art and cinemetic perfection and excellence this is a film every film fan must see I give it a perfect 10/10 If the story was a little tighter, The Rock could've a great action movie. Otherwise, it is still an entertaining movie that has a solid story, solid characters, and good action. I’m sure most fans of Michael Bay and action movies will enjoy this film, despite it’s shortcomings A perfect symphony of cliché and stereotype that Michael Bay's been trying like hell to recreate ever since. Literally every single shot dips liberally from the well of overuse, culminating in an early car chase with a little old lady, a roving gang of bicyclists, a dozen diving pedestrians in the road, no less than five instantly-combustible parked cars and a Lamborghini that leaps through a plate glass window.

Nic Cage and Sean Connery, no strangers to this type of picture, freely cast aside their inhibitions and embrace the cheese from word one. This, along with a straight-laced performance from Ed Harris, somehow validates the whole mess. The dialogue would have been deemed too unrealistic for a Hanna-Barbara cartoon, but through sheer force of will (plus a few blatant winks at the audience), that works too. Top of the mountain for the “insanely stupid action flick” boom of the mid '90s, The Rock is wildly fast-paced and thoroughly enjoyable in spite of itself. This is one of those good fun and action movies that is very nicely directed by Michael.

If you believe that, it's a start!") and has an amazing soundtrack. This ordinary action flick that at times is unintentionally funny is probably Michael Bay's best work. That's saying something.

833.rich_text:
The Ring The Ring Before you die, you see Horror Mystery Gore Verbinski Naomi Watts Martin Henderson David Dorfman Brian Cox Jane Alexander Lindsay Frost Amber Tamblyn Rachael Bella Daveigh Chase Shannon Cochran Journalist Rachel Keller investigates a strange videotape that may be behind the untimely deaths of four teenagers. There is an urban legend about this tape: the viewer will die seven days after watching it. Rachel tracks down the video... and watches it. Now she has just seven days to unravel the mystery of the Ring in order to save herself and her son. If you're planning to watch this movie alone on a Friday night, you'd better call a friend so you can watch it together. Because you definitely won't want to be alone afterward. It's that scary.

Whatever, its a clean 10 from me. Я бы сказал что неплохо, было интересно смотреть но точно не страшно, возможно атмосферу держал фильмец но хорором тяжело назвать Truly a masterpiece of horror. Everything about this film works; the acting, setting, storytelling, and color scheme are all sublime. Wasn’t expecting much coming into the film but left feeling impressed. Only negative is that it isn’t nearly as good upon rewatch since you already know how the mystery unfolds. I heard a lot about this movie and finally watched it, and I was pleasantly surprised by the detective part and the atmosphere, a good classic horror movie This film is average at best, the highlight being Watts’s convincing central performance. It is entertaining for the first half, however, the second half drags on and lacks any more gore or creepy visuals. In the gloomy Pacific northwest, an unlabeled VHS tape awaits the curious. After they press play, unlucky viewers are condemned to five minutes of eerie film school snippets, a breathy telephoned warning and an unexplained death within the week. Mourning one of the cassette’s latest victims, a tenacious newspaper reporter tracks down a copy, watches it, answers the phone and pursues the truth behind an urban legend. And then carelessly shares the curse with a few loved ones.

Maybe it’s because I’ve been watching so many iffy-to-bad horror movies lately, but The Ring really stands out. Not just as a good thriller, but as a top-quality film regardless of genre. It can scare without going over the top. Pose complex, troubling questions and see them through. Set a tone and stick to it. That last point is a particular strength: drenched with pervasive blue-green tones, dense mists and steady rain, this is a film with an excellent knack for atmosphere. It looks and feels like a headache brought on by too little sleep; a clinical hangover punctuated by a steady fluorescent hum. Which puts us in the same dazed, panicked head space as our protagonist, who certainly lacks for a good night’s rest during her increasingly hectic seven-day investigation. As the tragic ghost story unfolds, so does her own. Side by side, we learn about the cruel origins of that haunted tape and the tangled knot that’s become her private life. It’s an efficient, satisfying plot, one that succeeds on multiple fronts and doesn’t press the audience too far beyond the limits of their disbelief.

We catch some frights, but the camera never lingers. In fact, it often relegates the biggest, nastiest stuff to a spot on the fringe or a quick, fleeting glance. The Ring is an intelligent horror film, one which understands that what we thought we saw is often far worse than what we did. And when the time finally comes to pay out, it does that very well, too. Our climactic meeting with the dank, bedraggled little girl in the video - literally crawling through the CRT screen and shimmering with dirty static - is an unforgettable slice of cinematic trickery. The rare case of a big budget Hollywood horror movie that actually gets it, this one goes to some crazy places and most everything still makes sense in the end. Above average mystery drama/horror. 834.rich_text: Wish Wish Be careful what you wish for. Animation Family Fantasy Adventure Chris Buck, Fawn Veerasunthorn Ariana DeBose Chris Pine Alan Tudyk Angelique Cabral Victor Garber Natasha Rothwell Jennifer Kumiyama Harvey Guillén Niko Vargas Evan Peters Asha, a sharp-witted idealist, makes a wish so powerful that it is answered by a cosmic force – a little ball of boundless energy called Star. Together, Asha and Star confront a most formidable foe - the ruler of Rosas, King Magnifico - to save her community and prove that when the will of one courageous human connects with the magic of the stars, wondrous things can happen. A Wish Without Soul: The Failed Magic of Disney’s 100th Anniversary250114 (1.5)A cute mascot and a pretty fantasy world are never enough to guarantee the success of a Disney musical. In *Wish*, the story and characters lack distinct personalities, the plot progression feels forced, and worst of all—the music is incredibly underwhelming. The film is set in the Kingdom of Rosas, ruled by Magnifico, a sorcerer king who claims to grant the "wishes that make you who you are." However, he is a severe narcissist who only grants about 14 wishes a year, selectively choosing those that pose no threat to his power. When people hand over their wishes at age 18, they lose all memory of them, becoming hollow and lethargic shells of themselves. Asha, a young girl hoping to become the King's apprentice, discovers this dark reality when she asks for her 100-year-old grandfather Saba's wish to be granted. Her grandfather simply wants to create music that inspires others, yet Magnifico deems this "dangerous" and **** internal logic of the film is shaky at best. Asha, despite being told that solicitation is strictly forbidden, immediately begs for her grandfather's wish during her interview. When she eventually rebel’s against the King, the plot relies on weak coincidences. Even her friend Simon betrays her just to become a royal knight—a motivation that felt thin and unconvincing. The musical numbers, which should be the heart of a Disney film, are forgettable and lack the emotional punch of previous classics. The climax suggests that even after having their wishes stolen, people can simply make them glow in their hearts again by singing together, which felt like a lazy resolution. While the post-credits scene attempts to pay homage to Disney's legacy by revealing that Saba’s "inspiring music" is actually the iconic "When You Wish Upon a Star" from *Pinocchio*, it felt like a cheap emotional play. For a 100th-anniversary milestone, Disney should have focused on quality storytelling rather than just leaning on its past successes. Wish é um filme que tenta explorar um conceito interessante sobre desejos, poder e magia, mas acaba sendo mais uma animação esquecível do que um clássico da Disney. Embora tenha um visual agradável e boas intenções, o filme não consegue se destacar nem no desenvolvimento dos personagens, nem na profundidade da sua trama. No fim das contas, ele parece querer ser um filme com grandes lições de vida e emoções poderosas, mas acaba ficando no meio do caminho, sem nunca entregar o que promete. Se você for assistir, não espere mais do que um entretenimento leve e sem grandes surpresas.Nota: 5,5/10 – Regular. I really hated this movie. It made no sense, had a million plot holes, and was overall terrible. No thank you! If I had to describe this movie in one word, it would be "EMPTY".  Disney is drowning in greed, and it really shows. They scrapped all the good parts in the movie and replaced them with boring scenes, and all the songs sound like they were written with ChatGPT. There's no way "I'm a Star" was written by the same person who made "Let it Go". They replaced Star's original design (Starboy, he was going to be a shapeshifting human) with the little annoying thing he is now (probably to sell more merch). So yeah, this movie is terrible, don't waste your time watching it. I went in not expecting anything too grand based on the reception the initial release had, but I was actually pleasantly surprised- there is a decent movie in there straining against the Disney formula. There were definitely moments in this movie I was expecting- jokes too outdated to land, characters being ~quirky~, an animal sidekick for comedy relief. But the animal sidekick was actually pretty funny, and the cast of characters was wider then initially expected so their quirks were actually helpful in giving them personality. It did dip into blandness but I felt distinctly that it wasn’t for lack of trying- the people behind creating this loved it, I think. There was just a lot of the inescapable post 2010s Disney animated heroine movie aspects to it that, while not bad themselves, are just so typical that they’ve become boring. The music numbers where charming and fun but you can definitely tell the Lin Manual Miranda’s influence on the Disney sound certainly isn’t going anywhere. The villain was set up to have sympathetic motives and the fact that they didn’t explore that and just let him be evil along with a fun narcissistic song was really refreshing. Really loved the brief teenage revolution angle and the??? Way you could totally read this movie as an origin story for the fairy godmother. Overall the movie won me over. The cast do their best and there are some genuinely good ideas screaming to get out under a mire of wasted chances to make this something special given the premise of the movie they could have gone all out on pulling Disney IP from the last 100 years but the cameos we do get are dull and underutilised.There are some fun songs but none of them stick with you apart from perhaps the Chris Pine solo piece but it's nowhere in the same league as say the Elsa solo from **** looks nice enough but the character design follows the naturalistic / modern audience style of say the Lion King remake instead of the exaggerated styles of the original Lion King so the characters lack charisma or memorability with the noticeable exception of Magnifico (Chris Pine). The villain is actually Aisha lol. I wrote a huge review and it somehow got deleted so I am not going to waste my breath anymore. This film has no soul. Action Thriller Science Fiction Jonathan Mostow Arnold Schwarzenegger Nick Stahl Claire Danes Kristanna Loken Earl Boen David Andrews Carolyn Hennesy Jay Acovone Mark Famiglietti Moira Sinise It's been 10 years since John Connor saved Earth from Judgment Day, and he's now living under the radar, steering clear of using anything Skynet can trace. That is, until he encounters T-X, a robotic assassin ordered to finish what T-1000 started. Good thing Connor's former nemesis, the Terminator, is back to aid the now-adult Connor … just like he promised. Terminator 3: Rise of the Machines had a troubled production—James Cameron abandoned the project after disputes with Fox, leaving Jonathan Mostow to take over. The story follows John Connor years after Judgment Day: Sarah is dead, Skynet’s rise was delayed but inevitable, and a new female Terminator, the T-X, is sent to kill John’s future allies while a reprogrammed T-800 returns to protect him. Despite strong visual effects and Kristanna Loken’s effective performance as the T-X, the film lacks the emotional depth and intensity of its predecessors. It is a basic story and takes second place to the action. It should be story and action both together! I didn’t like the way that they made a joke out of the terminator. Still it was easy-going and fun. It is good that it is mostly set in the current time. Easily the weakest of the original trilogy but still a fun and campy ride and better than the Terminator films that came after this one. Was it really necessary to make such a poor third film ruining the first two perfect film? The clear demonstration that not everyone can take over the legacy of the greats. L’un de mes Terminator préférés ! c’est en effet le moins sérieux et le plus rocambolesque de la série et le plus drôle également… Que ce soit dans les dialogues ou les scènes d’action (très) improbables, c’est plein de jokes et Schwarzy en fait des tonnes ! il n’est pas le seul cela dit, car tous les personnages sont désormais d’authentiques caricatures (à l’insu de l’ignorance des scénaristes et du metteur en scène ou pas, là n’est pas la question).

Bref, on rigole beaucoup, on ne s’ennuie jamais et le scénario a un petit côté pré-Fallout très séduisant tout en évitant les discours parfois grandiloquents de Terminator 2. Quelques excellentes idées sont aussi fort judicieusement exploitées avec par exemple la terminatrice dont le développement et l’inventivité laissent bouche bée.

Finalement, pas mal de recul pour ce film d’action qui sait rester spectaculaire et perpétuer la mythologie de cette saga qui rebondit au rythme des retours vers le futur simple du passé antérieur.

Ce Terminator 3 est évidemment à prendre au second et même au troisième degré : il s’agit en vérité d’un film entier dédié au fan service et à ce titre il excelle d’une façon inattendue. On a par ailleurs une réalisation solide (Jonathan Mostow n’est pas un branque) dans l’ensemble malgré une grosse poursuite certes spectaculaire mais trop désordonnée et mal filmée. Le rythme reste soutenu de bout en bout et les effets spéciaux sont toujours au sommet ! Terminator 3 Rise of the Machines: How is it that this movie has better CGI then Resident Evil the movie. So we are going to start with the good first, Arnold as good as ever, I love the supporting cast, Nick Stahl as John Connor did a fantastic job and Claire Danes as Katie she was also great. The TX was a fantastic villain a female Terminator yeah it was cool. The special effects even looked good not over using CGI to the point of it looking gross but just enough to get your point across. Now the bad I hate the fact that Judgment Day was inevitable because that’s what the whole last movie was about stopping it, I don’t like how they killed off Sarah Connor but that’s a nitpick, but the main problem is it’s the same plot again, a evil Terminator goes to the past to kill Resistance members and the good Terminator comes back to protect the leaders, it’s the same plot as 1 and 2 it’s getting more tiresome. Overall Terminator 3 is a great sequel, great action, great characters, some good comedic moments it’s a good watch. Ranking Amazing. Very cliched and mediocre plot that ruins the masterpiece called Terminator 2. But I guess it will be kinda enjoyable if you ignore some of the flaws and if you're not a fan of this movie's predecessors. After two excellent films, Hollywood made the mistake of reviving the “Terminator” franchise and ruining it completely. But in this film we are still at an acceptable level of quality where things still seem to make some sense. In this film, we follow John Connor in another race to save himself from a TX machine, sent from the future, in the form of a woman, but with the mission of killing him and all the future human militia commanders. It is more of the same if we think about it and if we want to compare this film with its predecessors. But with less quality.

Overall, I liked the film, it honors its predecessors, but it is not able to do better, nor to do it differently. As has already happened, the film is essentially based on chases with immense destruction and shootings with increasingly powerful weaponry. There are several attempts to create comedic moments, but they don't always work and the dialogues are spiritless and sometimes irritating. And now that I mention it, one thing that caught my attention, and I don't know if it was just me, was the forced way in which the famous catchphrase “I'll be back” was used. And I don't even talk about monologues... I think some of them were perfectly expendable.

Again, as in other times, it is Arnold Schwarzenegger's performance that saves the film. As if he were a colossus, he is the one who carries it on his back. And in fact he is a great actor and is totally at ease in the role, which he already knows and immortalized. Nick Stahl is average and does reasonably in the role of Connor, but it did not convince me much. Better than him, Claire Danes is very good for the role she received and is the only actress who can keep up with Schwarzenegger in his work. Kristanna Loken is also quite good.

Technically, it is a very good film, but I still prefer “Terminator 2”, even though I know that the special effects used do not have the refinement of this film. I think the effects used in the film do their job well, but they can't be as surprising as those used in the older film. The action scenes, of course, are the strongest part of the film, and fill the measures with those who appreciate the genre, with immense destruction, explosions and twisted iron. Cinematography is very good, and makes good use of urban landscapes, the desert and scenes without light or in low light. Good editing and editing also help, and sets and costumes fulfill their role. The soundtrack makes good use of the leitmotiv of the franchise, but it does not stand out particularly.

836.title: 8 Mile

metadata.tagline: Every moment is another chance.

836.rich_text:
8 Mile 8 Mile Every moment is another chance. Drama Music Curtis Hanson Eminem Kim Basinger Mekhi Phifer Brittany Murphy Evan Jones Omar Benson Miller De'Angelo Wilson Eugene Byrd Taryn Manning Larry Hudson For Jimmy Smith, Jr., life is a daily fight just to keep hope alive. Feeding his dreams in Detroit's vibrant music scene, Jimmy wages an extraordinary personal struggle to find his own voice - and earn a place in a world where rhymes rule, legends are born and every moment… is another chance. Use to love this movie as a kid but the older i get the more i see the flaws with this movie. Its entertaining for sure but the final rap battle scene as a whole leaves a lot to be desired Great soundtrack, Lose Yourself is an amazing song, also the album that came from this movie has some incredible songs. 8mile the song is great and also Rap Game featuring D12 is one of the best D12 songs. The acting is also very good Eminem is surprisingly good as an actor and Anthony Mackie was good as Papa Doc and all of the supporting cast was really good As publicity-focused biopics go, 8 Mile is a well-executed example. Although it's self-serving at times, this is also an impressively open and honest take on Eminem's roots and the self-imposed wall of excuses he laid out for himself before catching so much as a whiff of ****. The plot outside of Mr. Marshall Mathers is fairly simplistic and limited, though, with most of the cast merely orbiting the star and reacting to his angry, frustrated outbursts.

I found the battle raps every bit as intense and exciting as a good action scene, and the choice to limit them to a few key moments was a smart move that doubled their importance. Eminem himself is startlingly good in the lead role; it may not be too much of a stretch to play yourself in the cinematic story of your own rise to fame, but I've certainly seen others try and fail. An authentic, street-smart piece of inspiration that offers a fresh take on a tired old tale. Una peli que sin duda marco mi infancia y definió mi gusto musical. A la fecha sigue siendo buenisima. Its way better than the 50 cent one and its probbably the greatest rap movie ever made;... but thats about it It's an average movie, the rap battles are very entertaining and I really liked Eminem's ascension to the top but it did feel slow at times, the story is directionless and the pacing is disjointed. Eminem turned out to be a pretty decent actor. I love battle raps. Honestly he's one of if not the best to ever do it! Surprisingly engaging drama with a talented cast and 'slice of life' feel to it reminiscent of juice only with an emphasis on the rapping and less on the gang culture. It's otherwise pretty standard fare for this genre but very enjoyable. The restrictions of the fictitious celebrity biopic are too great for "8 Mile." There were countless films about young musicians and their families, early promoters, first big breaks, etc., most of them with a wider scope and greater level of specificity than this one. This movie simply follows its hero until the moment he turns to leave, proving his star potential. His character, and in particular his stillness, are the centre of attention. The most significant moments occur when Eminem holds a microphone in his hand and waits in silence for inspiration to strike. In this film, Eminem expresses total imminence and pure potential with a new degree of conviction and clarity. Not commenting on the movie lol, just here to say that Lose yourself is the most overplayed annoying Eminem songs ever. There are so much better Em songs that this. Like, holy **** this song is so sentimental and corny. I can still see how this song could be catchy at some point, but all that's been left of the hook is vomit inducing and stomach churning verbal vomit. The word play and technical ability has been turned into a mess. And like I said, there or so many better Em songs that this!

837.title: The Irishman

metadata.tagline: His story changed history.

837.rich_text: The Irishman The Irishman His story changed history. Crime Drama History Martin Scorsese Robert De Niro Al Pacino Joe Pesci Harvey Keitel Ray Romano Bobby Cannavale Anna Paquin Stephen Graham Stephanie Kurtzuba Jack Huston Pennsylvania, 1956. Frank Sheeran, a war veteran of Irish origin who works as a truck driver, accidentally meets mobster Russell Bufalino. Once Frank becomes his trusted man, Bufalino sends him to Chicago with the task of helping Jimmy Hoffa, a powerful union leader related to organized crime, with whom Frank will maintain a close friendship for nearly twenty years. The Irishman is Scorsese looking back without easy nostalgia. Everything is here: the rise, the loyalty, the everyday violence of the mob world, but told from a different place, more tired, more lucid. This is not a film about how fast life moves in that environment, but about how slowly everything is paid for **** much of its runtime, the story unfolds with the ease of someone who has walked this path many times before. The conversations, gestures, and rituals of organized crime feel familiar, almost comforting for anyone who knows Scorsese’s cinema. But little by little, the film shifts its focus: power matters less than what is lost along the **** tone is essential. There is no romanticism or euphoria here. Violence is part of the routine, presented without emphasis, which makes it drier and more uncomfortable. Scorsese doesn’t frame crime as spectacle, but as a series of choices that quietly close doors, one after another, often without the protagonist **** cast is in absolute top form. It’s not about individual showmanship, but about how they support one another, building a sense of time passing and a world slowly fading. There’s an almost painful calm in the performances, as if everyone knows from the start where this is **** length can be debated, but it’s hard to imagine this story told any other way. The Irishman needs time for the erosion to be felt, for silence to weigh as much as gunshots once did. It’s a crepuscular, reflective, deeply honest film.More than a recap of his career, it feels like a farewell without ceremony. Scorsese doesn’t judge, explain, or forgive. He simply watches as time inevitably takes over everything. And in that final stretch, the film reaches a rare and lasting emotional power. It is too lengthy for me. And to be honest, nothings new inside it. I think the movie try to put as many typical gangsters pieces in a single story. The casts and acting also feels average except for Al Pacino performance. The Irishman là phim hình sự sử thi ám ảnh, theo chân sát thủ già hồi tưởng về quá khứ mafia, tình bạn và những tội lỗi không thể tha thứ. If i had to pick 1 movie to watch for the rest of my life this would be up there for one of the finalists. Its a long movie but it deserved every minute of your attention i rewatch this movie when im bored, when im happy when im tired it just never misses Really great cast and with that cast, plus Martin Scorsese and Steven Zaillian involved, my expectations were naturally high. Very high, in fact. But right from the beginning of the film, I was brought back down to earth and it didn’t get any better from **** first, I couldn’t quite put my finger on what went wrong with this movie. Was it the awful digital de-aging? The weak soundtrack? The excessive runtime? Yes, of course. But unfortunately, it was also Martin Scorsese’s surprisingly weak direction. The Irishman has absolutely a thrilling story despite it being long winded Martin Scorsese has certainly cooked up a delicious juicy Rib-Eye steak to remember. What an amazing journey! "The Irishman," directed by Martin Scorsese, is a masterwork of narrative, with Joe Pesci, Robert De Niro, and Al Pacino adding their grey hair and heat to this epic crime drama. It takes 3.5 hours, but believe me, it's well worth the effort. Just don't try to keep up with the amount of cigarettes smoked or the number of bodies found. Five stars, ten out of ten; I would watch it again, maybe with a sleep in between." Simply a colossal. I spent three hours and a half literally stuck on this majestic piece of art directed by Martin Scorsese and starring Robert De Niro, Al Pacino and Joe Pesci. Definitely would recommend this one. Perfect balance between action and drama. Killer in its category! It’s a masterpiece. I was not prepared for how devastated I would be seeing the stories of these three men unfold. The last scene between Pesci and De Niro had me in tears. De Niro doesn’t get enough credit for his performance in this film; all his “old age” scenes were absolutely devastating. It’s a damn shame all the de-aging hullabaloo distracted from his overall performance. Beyond the obvious comeuppance that characterized the 3rd act, it was also in a sense a poignant conclusion to Scorsese’s “gangster” filmography, and almost doubles as a meditation on his own life and career within the genre that has defined him.

metadata.tagline: When past meets future.

838.rich_text:
65 65 When past meets future. Action Adventure Science Fiction Scott Beck, Bryan Woods Adam Driver Ariana Greenblatt Chloe Coleman Nika King Brian Dare 65 million years ago, the only 2 survivors of a spaceship from Somaris that crash-landed on Earth, must fend off dinosaurs to reach the escape vessel in time before an imminent asteroid strike threatens to destroy the planet. What a total thrill ride from start to finish!  The plot and compressed but thorough character development. The concept of melding far flung futuristic but ancient sci-fi with prehistoric worlds, a father's search for redemption, and freakin' dinosaurs?! I cannot for the life of me understand how anyone didn't like this movie. This is an incredibly mid protector 'father/daughter' style movie masking itself as a cool alien dinosaur action flick that sadly doesn't deliver well on either end of those spectrums. Perhaps if there was more character development, or better action/tension scenes this movie could have been better. Der Film ist interessant gemacht, da hier aus der Sicht einer ausserirdischen Zivilisation (die eigentlich 1:1 der Menschen entsprechen) erzählt wird. Eines ihrer Raumschiffe muss notfallmässig auf der Erde landen, und dies zur Zeit der Dinosaurier. Noch schlimmer: Gerade zum Zeitpunkt vor dem Asteroideneinschlag. 
Der Survival-Aspekt ist okay Столкновение неизбежно
«65» — это американский научно-фантастический боевик американских режиссёров Скотта Бека и Брайана Вудса, главные роли в котором сыграли Адам Драйвер и Ариана Гринблатт. Фильм вышел на экраны в 2023 году.

Картинка: Атмосфера впечатляет: доисторические пейзажи, впечатляющие спецэффекты и динамичные столкновения с динозаврами создают напряжение. Жуки здесь действительно вызывают отвращение — именно то, что нужно. Однако местами картина выглядит немного неестественно, а в тёмных сценах трудно разглядеть детали, особенно на моём TN-мониторе.

Звук: Музыка в фильме усиливает напряжение в ключевых моментах. Титры сопровождаются музыкой, но она не запоминается. Рев динозавров хорош, но звуки бластеров звучат недостаточно мощно, в отличие от Star Wars.

Персонажи: Пилот Миллс и маленькая девочка Коа. Однако их образы получились поверхностными. Как зритель, я не успел по-настоящему проникнуться их историей, чтобы сопереживать им. Жаль.

Сюжет: История неплоха, так как на Земле 65 миллионов лет назад жили динозавры, которые примерно в это же время вымерли из-за астероида и ледникового периода, и началось наше время. Но исполнение оставляет желать лучшего. Сценарий предсказуем, а логические нестыковки и слабая проработка мира вызывают разочарование. Хотелось бы сразу почувствовать угрозу, ведь я уже знал, что летит астероид, а герои — нет. Хорошо было бы если сообщалось, что до столкновения осталось сколько то часов и т. д. Также хотелось бы увидеть больше интересных моментов, например, как появилась жизнь на Земле. Может быть, какие-то ДНК утекли — это, конечно, притянуто за уши, но всё же. Кроме астероида, который всё же порадовал, ничего интересного не было.

Итог: По постеру было ясно, что фильм будет посвящён динозаврам и их апокалипсису. Однако чего-то не хватило, чтобы по-настоящему привязаться к персонажам. С одной стороны, забавно, что они не понимали друг друга, но с другой — это же не наши люди, а представители другой цивилизации, и почему они не должны друг друга понимать? Исследовательская экспедиция оказалась не только в безвыходной ситуации, но и совершенно не была готова к ней: одна винтовка, никаких роботов или дронов! Зачем взяли ребёнка? Персонажи не только не понимают друг друга, но и не знают, как действовать. Пилота предупредили об опасности, но уже было поздно. В «Passengers » (2016) эта ситуация была обыграна интереснее, а моменты на земле напомнили «After Earth» (2013). Актёры тоже не впечатлили. Адам, например, запомнился ещё по «Star Wars» не очень, а девочка из-за непоняток в общении не оставила особого впечатления. Однако финал с динозавром из начала фильма был неплох. Люблю такие моменты, а так на один раз. Take the last of us, add some generic sci-fi and include a splash of Jurassic Park. What do you get? A really boring movie where nothing much happens. We’ve seen the bones of this creature before, for sure, but some terrific GGI monsters, swampy scares and Driver’s committed performance make 65 a snap-toothed popcorn multiplex movie which, at 93 minutes, is sprightly in comparison with its lumbering rivals. I just had to find out for myself who directed and wrote this film. To make a mental note that whoever it was has to be to most untalented moronic **** in the film industry. Scott Beck and Bryan Woods ladies and gentlemen, remember those names and stay the **** away. Virtually every scene you will be going, "this is dumb" or "why did he do that?" or "That was lame." or "FFS kill me now." Adam Driver in his most soulless and wooden performance EVER. It just boggles the mind that people this bad at story telling are making movies. I think this movie gets a little too much hate. Up until the very end where the premise became so outrageous, I was having a good time watching the movie. I thought Adam Driver did as good as you could with what the character was asked to do. I thought the story was interesting enough. Not groundbreaking or revolutionary, but good enough. The action and suspense were well done too. This isn't going to redefine any genres, but I think it's worth a watch if you just want a mildly entertaining movie to watch one evening. IN A NUTSHELL:
The dramatic story is about an astronaut who crash-lands on a mysterious planet, only to discover he’s not alone.
The film is both written and directed by Scott Beck and Bryan Woods, who also worked together on the film Haunt.  The movie was shot in only 40 days!  Another thing that’s unusual about this movie is that it only had one press screening before its release, less than 24 hours before it was released worldwide!  

THINGS I LIKED:
I adore Adam Driver.  He’ll win an Oscar someday.  I really wanted him to win for his performance in the film Marriage Story, but Joaquin Phoenix definitely deserved the Oscar for what he accomplished in the movie Joker.  Did you know Adam Driver was a Marine?  He gets to use some of his weapons training in this movie.
Ariana Greenblatt is such a little treasure and totally adorable.  I think I first saw her in Love and Monsters, a movie I really enjoyed and highly recommend for its creativity and humor.  She is a great, young actress with a very bright future in Hollywood.
Some of the filming took place in the Kisatchie National Forest in Louisiana.
Koa is a Hawaiian word used in the movie that means “warrior.”
There are moments when you feel like you’re watching another Jurassic Park movie.
The title gets its name from the fact that we get to see the earth 65 million years ago.
The emotional heft is a bit cliched, yet still very effective, reminding us that family is everything.
Very good and believable special effects and CGI.
In a year slated to be filled with sequels and franchise additions, the fact that this movie is original is one of its strengths.
Critics hate this movie, but I really enjoyed it!
An interesting element of the film is that the two leads don’t speak the same language and have to figure out how to communicate in other ways.  

THINGS I DIDN’T LIKE:
The plot is pretty simple, but that doesn’t make it a bad movie.
Not enough dinosaur moments.  A few of the dino scenes look like they’re straight out of Jurassic Park like when we see T-rex’s face slowly emerge from a dramatic waterfall.
I would like to have seen more of Chloe Coleman in the film.  She’s another young starlet who is fantastic.  I loved her in My Spy.
Sometimes, it’s hard to see what’s happening in the dark, cave scenes.  They’ll be hard to see on small devices if you stream the movie.   

TIPS FOR PARENTS:    
We see some blood and gore.
Some dinosaurs die brutal, disgusting deaths.
Violence
We see some dead bodies.
Kids will be excited to see some dinosaurs!
There are some scary, intense moments that could frighten young children.
People in perilous situations.
Lots of destruction The film with the short and meaningless title "65" surprises with good CGI's, a good story and a dense, exciting atmosphere. Not a milestone in SF, but absolutely suitable for a cozy movie evening.

839.rich_text:
Extraction 2 Extraction 2 Prepare for the ride of your life. Action Thriller Crime Sam Hargrave Chris Hemsworth Golshifteh Farahani Adam Bessa Tornike Gogrichiani Tornike Bziava Tinatin Dalakishvili Andro Japaridze Justin Howell Idris Elba Olga Kurylenko Back from the brink of death, highly skilled commando Tyler Rake takes on another dangerous mission: saving the imprisoned family of a ruthless gangster. It was not bad, feel like it trying to build up for something so they pull back a little. the previous movie have better exploration but this movie is not bad. I didn't like the boy perhaps i didn't understand his character but he have a decision issue. Extraction II falls squarely into the category of unnecessary sequels that are still watchable. The kind of movie that works as a time-killer but doesn’t offer much in the way of depth.

The story picks up right where the prequel left off. Tyler Rake basically comes back from the dead for another mission: to rescue—or rather, extract—his ex-sister-in-law from a prison run by the Nagazi, a powerful Georgian crime syndicate.

The plot follows the usual formula for this genre: force the protagonist into a situation that dredges up pieces of his past, trying to build an emotional connection to the external chaos unfolding around him. Extraction II is easy to follow and even easier to predict. What saves it are the action scenes and the cast.

One standout moment in Act One features a 21-minute continuous shot. It’s surreal to watch—intense, gripping, and technically impressive. A technique that gained fame after showing up in John Wick 3 (or was it **** actors themselves are top-tier professionals. Nothing to complain about there.

Overall, Extraction II is fine for casual viewing, the kind of film that doesn’t tax your brain with complications or nuance. A smooth ride that feels tailor-made for a Sunday evening of mental decay. Acceptable. Like its predecessor, it's an ok film with a fairly generic storyline! That said, the action is ok, some of the acting is also ok. Nothing special though.  Watch when you're bored! Extraction review A
Starring Chris Hemsworth,Golshifteh Farahani,Tornike Gogrichiani.
Rating=7.5/10
